(AWS), "Demonstrating a long-coherence dual-rail erasure qubit using tunable transmons", PRX 14, 011051 (arXiv:2307.08737, 2023-07-17): erasure probability 2.19(2)×10⁻³ per single-qubit gate, residual (non-erasure) errors ~40× lower, millisecond-scale coherence inside the code space, mid-circuit erasure detection adding < 0.1% dephasing per check

YALE-DUALRAIL-CAVITY-2023.text: Chou et al. (Yale), "Demonstrating a superconducting dual-rail cavity qubit with erasure-detected logical measurements", Nature Physics 20, 1454 (arXiv:2307.03169, 2023-07-06): over 99% of cavity decay events detected as erasures; logical SPAM error at the 0.01% level; decay ≈0.2% per µs; phase errors 6× rarer than decay; bit flips at least 140× rarer

YALE-DOUBLEPOST-2023-11.text: Koottandavida et al. (Yale), PRL 132, 180601 (arXiv:2311.04423, 2023-11-08): double-post superconducting cavity dual-rail qubit with erasure rate 3.981 ± 0.003 ms⁻¹ against residual in-codespace dephasing up to 0.17 ms⁻¹ — a ≈23× hierarchy

PSIQ-OMEGA-METRICS-2025.text: PsiQuantum Omega (Nature, 2025) uses path-encoded (dual-rail) photonic qubits — "we prepare a path-encoded qubit using a heralded photon and two-mode interferometers": single-mode SiN waveguide loss 1.8 ± 0.2 dB/m, splitter loss 0.5 ± 0.2 mdB, BTO switch insertion loss 100 mdB, median on-chip SNSPD efficiency 93.4%, fusion Bell fidelity 99.22 ± 0.12%, chip-to-chip Bell 99.72 ± 0.04%, SPAM 99.98 ± 0.01%, fibre-to-chip 52 ± 12 mdB, ~2 K — NOTE the main report's "waveguide loss 0.5 dB/m" is not the single-mode SiN figure and is unreconciled

OQC-ERASURE-REVIEW-2026-01.text: Violaris, Henaut, Wills, Consani, Friel, Vlastakis (Oxford Quantum Circuits), "Developments in superconducting erasure qubits for hardware-efficient quantum error correction", arXiv:2601.02183 (2026-01-05): surface-code threshold 50% with perfect erasure location vs ≈19% for depolarising noise; 5.2× improvement in tolerable Pauli rate; ≥2× threshold with imperfect checks; biased-erasure thresholds 2–5× higher; near-term target heralded erasure < ~4×10⁻³ with residual Pauli ~10⁻⁴ — first industrial-group review of erasure qubits from a UK vendor

QUTRIT-ERASURE-2026-04.text: Liu, Wang, Wang, Badbaria, Puri, Wang (UMass Amherst / Yale), "Hardware-efficient erasure qubits with superconducting transmon qutrits", arXiv:2604.08672 (2026-04-09): one transmon plus one ancilla instead of two rails; erasure lifetime 45 µs, logical T1 > 500 µs and T2 > 300 µs (XY4) post-selected against physical T1^ge ≈ 55 µs and T2E ≈ 75 µs; false positives ~2.0%, false negatives 6.0–8.0%; single-qubit gate infidelity ~4×10⁻⁴; bit-flip budget ~3.0×10⁻³ per cycle

DUALRAIL-CAT-2026-07.text: Biswas, Sharma, Salvador, Wang, Granath, Udupa, Ferrini, "Bias-preserving gates and quantum error correction with dual-rail cat codes", arXiv:2607.00786 (2026-07-01): proposes a deterministic single-photon-loss correction protocol in which all logical operations preserve the erasure-biased noise structure; theory only, no hardware demonstration, no quantitative threshold given in the abstract

DWAVE-DR-NAMING-2026-08.text: D-Wave/Quantum Circuits gate-model roadmap is stated as named dual-rail systems: DR17 (17 dual-rail physical qubits, 2× logical error reduction, "hardware-level erasure tracking") in 2026, DR49 (20× reduction) 2027, DR181 (2,000× error-suppression factor) 2028, 10-logical-qubit system 2030, 100-logical-qubit system with > 1 M logical operations 2032, target Λ = 10 [P]

ORCA-DUALRAIL-PATENT-2025.text: ORCA Computing Limited US 12,437,225, "Linear-optical encoded GHZ measurements and fault-tolerant quantum computation and communication" (filed 2023-10-16, granted 2025-10-07); related application US 2024/0256939 (published 2024-08-01) — the only photonic dual-rail patent family surfaced by a Justia search; no Yale, Quantum Circuits, Amazon or PsiQuantum patent appears under the query "dual rail qubit"

DUALRAIL-LINEAGE.text: Dual-rail as an error-correcting encoding predates superconducting qubits: Chuang & Yamamoto, "Simple quantum computer", Phys. Rev. A 52, 3489 (arXiv:quant-ph/9505011, 1995) — "By using a dual-rail qubit representation as a simple form of error correction, our machine can tolerate some amount of decoherence"; Knill, Laflamme & Milburn, arXiv:quant-ph/0006088 (2000-06-20), Nature 409, 46 (2001), built linear-optical QC on path-encoded photons

WILLOW-QEC-2024-12.text: Google Quantum AI, "Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold", Nature 638, 920 (arXiv:2408.13687, published 2024-12-09): Λ = 2.14 ± 0.02 per two distance steps (d=3→5→7), d=7 logical error 0.143 ± 0.003% per cycle, memory 2.4 ± 0.3× the best physical qubit, 1.1 µs QEC cycle, 10⁶ cycles sustained at d=5 with a 63 µs mean real-time decoder latency, error floor ≈10⁻¹⁰ set by roughly hourly correlated events [D]

GOOGLE-SC-2023-02.text: Google Quantum AI, "Suppressing quantum errors by scaling a surface code logical qubit", Nature 614, 676–681 (2023-02-22): distance-5 logical error 2.914(16)% per cycle versus distance-3 average 3.028(23)% — the first below-threshold scaling data and the origin of "surface code demonstrated since 2023" [D]

YOKED-SURFACE-2023.text: Gidney, Newman, Brooks, Jones (Google), "Yoked surface codes", arXiv:2312.04522 (2023-12-07): surface-code patches concatenated into a sparse outer parity-check code "nearly triple" logical qubits per physical qubit; at p = 10⁻³ and 10⁻¹³–10⁻¹⁴ target error, ≈1,500 physical per logical plain, ≈800 with 1D yokes, ≈600 with 2D yokes; no connectivity beyond a nearest-neighbour square grid; figures read from a secondary rendering, arxiv html returned HTTP 429 [S]

SURFACE-TERAQUOP-650.text: Gidney, Jones (Google), arXiv:2312.08813 (2023-12-14): under uniform depolarizing noise at 0.1%, the middle-out colour-code circuit reaches a teraquop footprint of 1,250 qubits versus 650 for surface codes decoded by correlated matching — the source of the "650 physical per logical" figure [S]

RIVERLANE-LCD-2025-12.text: Ziad, Zalawadiya, Topal, Camps, Gehér, Stafford, Turner (Riverlane), "Local clustering decoder as a fast and adaptive hardware decoder for the surface code", Nature Communications 16, 11048 (2025-12-17): under 1 µs per round on FPGA up to d=17 using ≈6% of the logic LUTs and ≈3% of the flip-flops of a Xilinx VU19P; 4× fewer physical qubits (d=33→17) for one million error-free operations under leakage-dominated circuit noise; thresholds 0.55% (unweighted hardware LCD), ≈0.65% (weighted software LCD), 0.7% (PyMatching MWPM) [D]

ALPHAQUBIT-2024-11.text: Bausch et al. (Google DeepMind / Google Quantum AI), "Learning high-accuracy error decoding for quantum processors", Nature 635, 834–840 (2024-11-20): recurrent transformer decoder for the surface code; on Sycamore data 2.901(23)×10⁻² at d=3 (vs tensor-network 3.028(23)×10⁻²) and 2.748(15)×10⁻² at d=5 (vs 2.915(16)×10⁻²); ~25% better error suppression than correlated matching at simulated d=11 [D]

RIVERLANE-FUNDING.text: Riverlane Series C $75 M announced 2024-08-06 (Planet First Partners lead; ETF Partners, EDBI, Cambridge Innovation Capital, Amadeus, NSSIF, Altair); customers named: Rigetti, Alice & Bob, QuEra, Infleqtion, Atlantic Quantum, Oak Ridge, UK NQCC. Riverlane's 2026-03-12 roadmap release instead states "Series C: $85 million in 2024" and "$120 million+" private funding — CONFLICT, no extension release found; earlier £2.1 M Horizon Europe EIC Transition grant (project SkyTALE, with Qblox) 2024-05-01 [C]

RIVERLANE-ROADMAP-2026-03.text: Riverlane QEC Technology Roadmap (2026-03-12): megaquop (10⁶ reliable operations) before the end of the decade, gigaquop early 2030s, teraquop from 2033; claims over 20 partnerships with quantum-computer makers and national labs and "over 60% of the world's quantum computer companies"; assumes the surface code with the Local Clustering Decoder on superconducting qubits [C][R]

QBLOX-RIVERLANE-2026-03.text: Qblox and Riverlane closed-loop QEC demonstration announced 2026-03-17 (APS Global Physics Summit): 250 physical qubits and one logical qubit, sub-microsecond feedback between detection and correction, up to 10,000 QuOps, using Riverlane's Deltaflow 2 and Deltakit with Qblox control hardware; Oxford Quantum Circuits and NVIDIA named as collaborators [C]

SURFACE-CODE-PATENTS.text: Google LLC US 12,518,194 "Surface codes with densely packed gauge operators" (filed 2023-11-20, granted 2026-01-06) — gauge operators and composite stabilizers to run the code on lattices with non-functional qubits; Riverlane Ltd GB 2641501 A "Quantum decoder" (Ziad, Zalawadiya, Barber, Skorić; filed 2024-05-31, published 2025-12-10) — grouped processing elements running clustering sequentially on the decoding hypergraph in hardware

OMG-BLUEPRINT-2021.text: Allcock, Campbell, Chiaverini, Chuang, Hudson, Moore, Ransford, Roman, Sage, Wineland, "omg blueprint for trapped ion quantum computing with metastable states", Applied Physics Letters (2021): optical-metastable-ground architecture in which one ion species supplies qubit, ancilla and coolant via three manifolds; origin of the "omg" name (exact APL volume/page not fetched)

OREGON-MSTABLE-ION-2024-11.text: Quinn, Gregory, Moore, Brudney, Metzner, Ritchie, O'Reilly, Wineland, Allcock (University of Oregon), "High-fidelity entanglement of metastable trapped-ion qubits with integrated erasure conversion", arXiv:2411.12727 (2024-11-19), Phys. Rev. A (2026, doi:10.1103/p3cy-8yjk): qubit in the 40Ca+ D5/2 manifold (mJ = +5/2, +3/2), geometric phase gate ~400 us from 976 nm Raman beams detuned -43 THz; Bell fidelity 97.73% raw, 98.61% SPAM-corrected, 99.16% erasure-subtracted; ~94% of spontaneous-Raman-scattering errors and nearly all decay errors detected, roughly half of the total error budget converted; arXiv HTML gives 98.56%/99.14% and -44 THz - minor conflict

OREGON-OMG-MIDCIRCUIT-2026-08.text: Brudney, Burns, Gregory, Ritchie, Wineland, Allcock, O'Reilly (Oregon), "Mid-circuit ground-state cooling and ancilla readout in the omg architecture", arXiv:2608.13181 (2026-08-13): mixed metastable/ground-state Coulomb crystal; global motional mode cooled to the ground state by dissipative operations on the ground qubit and non-destructive metastable-qubit readout by quantum logic spectroscopy, both without disturbing metastable coherence; no timing or fidelity figures in the abstract

IONQ-QLDPC-BREAKEVEN-2026-06.text: Tham, Goldman, Debnath, Nielsen, Pisenti, Wright, Gamble, Delfosse (IonQ), "Breakeven demonstration of quantum low-density parity-check codes", arXiv:2606.06455 (2026-06-04): 4 logical qubits in 18 trapped-ion physical qubits, logical memory lifetime 3.95 ± 0.68 s vs 3.3 ± 0.9 s for the best physical qubit (leakage post-selected), logical error rate up to 9x better than the previous superconducting BB-code demonstration; first qLDPC break-even on any hardware; no logical two-qubit gate reported [D]

ZHEJIANG-BB-KUNLUN-2025-05.text: Wang, Lu, Zhang et al. (Zhejiang University, Tsinghua, Shanghai Qi Zhi), "Demonstration of low-overhead quantum error correction codes": [[18,4,4]] bivariate bicycle and [[18,6,3]] qLDPC codes on the 32-qubit Kunlun superconducting processor (18 data + 14 check; 84 tunable couplers, long-range links up to 6.5 mm, degree-6 torus, air-bridge crossovers), up to 6 syndrome cycles; (8.91 ± 0.17)% and (7.77 ± 0.12)% per logical qubit per cycle — above the ~0.8-1% physical error, i.e. NOT break-even [D]

GROSSCODE-FPGA-2025-10.text: Maurer, Buehler, Kroener, Haverkamp, Mueller, Vandeth, Johnson (IBM), "Real-time decoding of the gross code memory with FPGAs", arXiv:2510.21600 (2025-10-24): Relay-BP for the [[144,12,12]] gross code on FPGA, belief-propagation iteration time 24 ns, average decoding time under 1 microsecond per cycle for physical error probabilities below 3e-3, reduced-precision arithmetic matching floating-point logical error performance; simulation-driven hardware study, not a decode of live syndromes [S]

HELIOS-ICEBERG-2026-02.text: Quantinuum, "Computing with many encoded logical qubits beyond break-even" (arXiv:2602.22211, 2026-02): two-level concatenated iceberg codes [[(k1+2)(k2+2), k1k2, 4]] on the 98-qubit Helios; largest fully-executed QEC cycle [[80,48,4]] with 48 corrected logical qubits, average QEC-cycle infidelity per logical qubit upper-bounded at 4×10⁻⁵ (zero logical errors in 5,000 shots per basis), logical gate infidelity (1.0–1.2)×10⁻⁴ vs ~8×10⁻⁴ physical 2Q, acceptance 0.62(2); single-level iceberg QED [[k+2,k,2]] up to 94 logical qubits [D]

TESSERACT-16-6-4.text: The tesseract colour code is [[16,6,4]] (doubly-even self-dual 4D CSS code from the [16,5,8] first-order Reed–Muller code), with subsystem variant [[16,4,2,4]] used in the Quantinuum demonstration; full logical Clifford group in depth-one two-local circuits, twelve addressable logical CZ pairs. Microsoft Quantum + Quantinuum, Nature 654 (2026-06-10): 11×–800× logical-error improvement, graph states on up to 12 logical qubits, 5 correction rounds. Same code carries Harvard's 96 logical qubits on 448 atoms. NOTE: the graph/technology-graph record value [[16,4,4]] is an error

ICEBERG-QUANTUM-SEED-2026-02.text: Iceberg Quantum (founded out of the University of Sydney; Felix Thomsen CEO, Larry Cohen CSO, Samuel Smith CTO): $2 M pre-seed 2025-03-24 (Blackbird lead, LocalGlobe) and $6 M seed 2026-02-13 (LocalGlobe lead, Blackbird, DCVC), ~$8 M cumulative; hardware partners PsiQuantum (2025-03), Oxford Ionics (2025-07), Diraq (2025-08); "Pinnacle" qLDPC architecture (arXiv:2602.11457) claims RSA-2048 with fewer than 100,000 physical qubits at p=10⁻³, 1 µs cycle, 10 µs reaction time

SEEQC-MK-SFQ-2026-03.text: Jordan, Bernhardt, Rahamim, Kirichenko et al. (Seeqc Inc. Elmsford NY + Seeqc UK London), "A quantum computer controlled by superconducting digital electronics at millikelvin temperature", Nature Electronics 2026-03-10: qubits and SFQ control integrated in ONE multi-chip module by flip-chip bonding, digital demultiplexing fans one digital input to several qubits, single-qubit fidelity "exceeding 99%" and up to 99.9%; the five-qubit count, 10 mK, "nanowatts per qubit" and "absence of detectable quasiparticle poisoning" come from press coverage, not the abstract [D]/[C]

SEEQC-FUNDING.text: SEEQC: spun out of Hypres in 2019 with IP and foundry infrastructure from >$100 M of prior Hypres investment; Series A $22.4 M 2020-09-16 led by EQT Ventures (FAM AB, M Ventures $5 M, BlueYard, NewLab Ventures, Partnership Fund for NYC), cumulative >$29 M incl. $6.8 M seed; $30 M round announced 2025-01-16 with no named lead (SIP Global Partners, NordicNinja, Booz Allen Ventures, EQT, M Ventures, BlueYard, FAM); owns a commercial multi-layer superconductor foundry in Elmsford NY plus sites in London and Naples

SFQ-QP-POISONING-2023.text: Liu, Ballard, Olaya, Schmidt, Biesecker et al. (Wisconsin, Syracuse, NIST, CU Boulder, LLNL), PRX Quantum 4, 030310 (2023-07-24): SFQ driver on a separate die joined by In-bump bonds, error per Clifford 1.2(1)% of which 0.96(2)% incoherent and attributed to photon-mediated quasiparticle poisoning via resonant mm-wave antenna modes; authors project 0.1% (resonant) / 0.01% (complex sequences) if the SFQ driver bandwidth is limited [D]

SHUTTLE-CZ-DELFT-2026-05.text: Controlled-phase gate between two *moving* (shuttled) spins in Si/SiGe (Matsumoto et al., Vandersypen group, QuTech/TU Delft, Nature 653, 2026-05-06): 98.86 +/- 0.29% average two-qubit fidelity, 240 nm of motion (120 nm per qubit), 58 ns gate at 1.8 m/s, six-dot device [D]

SHUTTLE-PARITY-DELFT-2026-07.text: Weight-four parity checks with a mobile ancilla spin qubit (Undseth et al., QuTech/TU Delft, Nature 655, 1160-1166, 2026-07-29): five-qubit device, 97.7(1)% fidelity per 1.2 um round-trip shuttle, Z-parity 72.2(6)%, X-parity 67.0(7)%; dephasing during shuttling and idling ~1/4 of total error, exchange-interaction noise dominant [D]

ARQUE-SYSTEMS-2022.text: ARQUE Systems GmbH: spin-off of Forschungszentrum Juelich and RWTH Aachen founded 2022-09 by Hendrik Bluhm and three colleagues; commercialises patented conveyor-mode spin shuttling (QuBus / SpinBus); first five-qubit processor being installed at Juelich Supercomputing Centre; funding amount and investors undisclosed as of 2026-09-03 [C]

MAGIC-CULTIVATION-2025-12.text: Google Quantum AI, "Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor" (Rosenfeld, Gidney, Roberts, Morvan, Lacroix et al., arXiv:2512.13908, 2025-12-15): magic-state fidelity 0.9999(1) retaining 8% of attempts, error reduced 40x, including code-switching into a surface code and a fault-tolerant protocol bounding the fidelity [D]

MAGIC-CODESWITCH-2025-06.text: Quantinuum (Daguerre, Blume-Kohout, Brown, Hayes, Kim), "Experimental demonstration of high-fidelity logical magic states from code switching", Phys. Rev. X 15, 041008 (arXiv:2506.14169, 2025-06-17): first code switching between colour codes, [[15,1,3]] quantum Reed-Muller to [[7,1,3]] Steane, logical magic-state infidelity at most 5.1(2.7)x10^-4 at 82.58% success, 2.7x better than physical [D]

MAGIC-MSD-NEUTRAL-2025-07.text: Cantu et al. (QuEra, Harvard, MIT), "Experimental demonstration of logical magic state distillation", Nature 645, 620-625 (2025-07-14): first logical-level 5-to-1 magic-state distillation, on d=3 and d=5 colour codes, on a reconfigurable neutral-atom processor; reports improvement of output over input logical fidelity (no absolute output infidelity in the abstract) [D]

QPHOX-SERIESA-2024-01.text: QphoX (Delft, NL) raised a €8 M Series A announced 2024-01-17, led by QDNL Participations with the EIC Fund, Quantonation, Speedinvest, High-Tech Gründerfonds and Delft Enterprises; €2 M seed in 2021, cumulative €10 M; the only pure-play microwave-optical transducer ("quantum modem") company, no later round disclosed as of 2026-09-03 [C]

NUQ-SERIESA-2025-12.text: Nu Quantum (Cambridge, UK) raised a $60 M Series A announced 2025-12-10, led by National Grid Partners with Gresham House Ventures, Morpheus Ventures, Amadeus Capital Partners, IQ Capital, Ahren Capital, Cambridge Enterprise Ventures, East Innovate, NSSIF and Sumitomo/Presidio Ventures; roadmap: Qubit-Photon Interface 2024, Quantum Networking Unit 2025; no entanglement rate or fidelity published; does not perform microwave-optical conversion itself [C]

TRANSDUCER-GAP-2026.text: Microwave-optical transduction state of the art (as tabulated in review arXiv:2605.26976, 2026-05): best internal efficiency 99.5% with total efficiency 15% and added noise 0.16 photons at 60 mK (Sahu 2022, bulk LiNbO3 electro-optic); best added noise 0.12 photons at 30 MHz bandwidth (Warner 2025, TFLN); best total efficiency 47% (Higginbotham 2018) with noise far above one photon; the integrated device family used for optical qubit readout runs at total efficiency 3e-6 with 6 added photons (Weaver 2024, QphoX, tabulated in arXiv:2505.00542). Useful regime requires eta > 1/2 with N_add << 1; IBM (arXiv:2503.10842) requires "3 orders of magnitude in added noise, efficiency, and repetition rates" for 99.7% remote gates at MHz rates, while QphoX/IST Austria argue >99% Bell fidelity is reachable with today's devices by heralding plus distillation - unresolved

HARVARD-CZ-2026-04.text: Evered, Xu, Li, Geim, Bonilla Ataides, Kalinowski, Bluvstein, Maskara, Kokail, Greiner, Vuletic, Lukin (Harvard/MIT), "High-fidelity entangling gates and nonlocal circuits with neutral atoms", arXiv:2604.25987 (2026-04-28): Rydberg-blockade CZ 99.854(4)% raw / 99.941(3)% loss-post-selected, stable ~10 h without recalibration; Rb 53S_1/2, two-photon 420 nm + 1015 nm at 7.8 GHz intermediate detuning, peak Rabi 2pi x 17 MHz; error budget dominated by atom loss 0.087(5)% per gate (~60% of total), leakage to other m_F 0.008(1)% per atom per gate; authors project 99.9-99.95% from better T2*, suppressed coupling to a nearby Rydberg level and higher laser power [D]

QUERA-GEMINI-SPEC-2026-09.text: QuEra "Gemini" product page (accessed 2026-09-03): 260 physical qubits, global 2-qubit gate fidelity 99.2%, global 1-qubit 99.9%, local 1-qubit 99.7%, SPAM 99.7%, repetition rate 1 shot/second; no availability date, deployment site or price disclosed [C]

RYDBERG-CEILING-2026-08.text: Wang, Wang, Li, Wang, Liang, Yan (Information Engineering University), "Neutral Atom Quantum Computing: Principles, Routes, Progress, and Challenges", arXiv:2608.05010 (2026-08-05): argues the standard blockade CZ has a "physical limit of 99.9%" from spontaneous Rydberg emission (0.05-0.1%) + laser phase noise (0.1-0.2%) + thermal motion (~0.1%), and that breaking the bottleneck needs new mechanisms (Forster-resonance gates). CAUTION: the same review tabulates a 2025 USTC CZ of 99.84% that no primary source corroborates [P]

ALPHAQUBIT2-2026-07.text: AlphaQubit2 is named and described as "a scalable and real-time neural decoder for topological quantum codes" in Sivak, Morvan, Broughton et al. (Google Quantum AI), "Reinforcement learning control of quantum error correction", Nature 655 (8124), published 2026-07-08 (preprint arXiv:2511.08493, 2025-11-11): it decoded the distance-7 surface code in real time for the record average logical error 7.72(9)x10^-4 per cycle; the distance-5 colour code used the search-based Tesseract decoder at 8.19(14)x10^-3 per cycle; no Lambda reported for the d=7 run; no stand-alone AlphaQubit2 publication exists as of 2026-09-03 [D]

NN-DECODER-FPGA-2026-05.text: Yang, Sun, Wu, Zhang, Jiang, Linpeng, Zhou, Chu, Niu, Zhong, Liu, Yu (International Quantum Academy Shenzhen / SUSTech / Peking University / Hefei National Laboratory), "Real-time Surface-Code Error Correction Using an FPGA-based Neural-Network Decoder", arXiv:2605.04892 (2026-05-06): first closed-loop neural decoding on a superconducting processor - LSTM with 32 hidden units, 6-bit quantised weights, separate X/Z decoders on an AMD Kintex-7 XC7K410T; 124 ns decode latency, 184 ns throughput period, 550 ns deterministic closed loop (222 ns acquisition + 148 ns logic + 180 ns electronics) inside a 1.25 us QEC cycle; distance-3 surface code on a 66-qubit chip (17-qubit subset), real-time 6.9(2)% per round vs offline MWPM 7.2(2)%; authors put current FPGA parts at approximately distance-13 ceiling [D]

IBM-MODCRYO-2026-08.text: IBM coupled two modular cryogenic cell prototypes (blog 2026-08-19): 0.53 m² wiring area and 2.75 m³ vacuum chamber volume per cell, cells expected to hold "thousands of qubits each"; l-couplers described as "one meter scale" and "first demonstrated in 2024" (on Flamingo); no qubits and no fidelity in the coupled-cell result [C]

RIGETTI-CHIPLET-LADDER.text: Rigetti chiplet tiling ladder: 36 q from four 9-qubit chiplets at median 2Q 99.5% (2025-07-16, a 2× error cut vs 84-q Ankaa-3) → 108 q from twelve 9-qubit chiplets at median 2Q 99.1%, 1Q 99.9%, ~60 ns gates (GA 2026-04-07); the 40-basis-point drop across the tripling is unattributed in both releases [C]

IBM-NIGHTHAWK-9MODULE-2028.text: IBM roadmap detail (blog 2025-06-10): Nighthawk to "connect up to 9 modules with l-couplers to realize 1,080 connected qubits" by 2028; Cockatoo (2027) to demonstrate entanglement between modules via the universal adapter; c-couplers = intra-chip, l-couplers = chip-to-chip [R]

SNSPD-EFF-RECORDS.text: Single-photon detector efficiency records: fibre-coupled system detection efficiency 98.0 ± 0.5% at 1550 nm (Reddy, Nerem, Nam, Mirin, Verma, NIST, Optica 7(12), 2020-11-23); on-chip (waveguide-integrated) efficiency 99.73% for a cascaded NbN pair and 97.33% for a single detector at 1.5 K, 1550 nm, 100 nm wide / 5 nm thick (Wu et al., Nanjing University RISE + Peking University + Hefei National Lab, Light: Sci. Appl., 2025-10-17); the two are NOT comparable — on-chip excludes fibre-to-chip coupling; power-meter calibration uncertainty is 2-5%, comparable to the gap between them [D]

SNSPD-VENDORS-2026.text: Merchant single-photon-detector supply base as of 2026-09-03: Single Quantum (Delft NL, 400th SNSPD system shipped to Q*Bird 2026-07-04 [P]), ID Quantique (Geneva CH, acquired by IonQ, closed 2025-05-06), Photon Spot (Monrovia CA, sells its own Cryospot 4/4TS/5 cryostats, >90% QE, sub-100 ps jitter [C]), Quantum Opus (MI, Opus One >=90% at 1310/1550 nm, >2 K, photon-number resolving under exclusive licence to US 11,274,962 B2 [C]), Scontel (Moscow RU, descendant of the Gol'tsman MSPU group); NIST Boulder and JPL hold the records but sell nothing; PsiQuantum builds detectors in-house on 300 mm GlobalFoundries. No detector vendor has disclosed a funding round or revenue

SNSPD-CAMERA-400K.text: Oripov, Rampini, Allmaras, Shaw, Nam, Korzh, McCaughan (NIST Boulder, CU Boulder, JPL), "A superconducting nanowire single-photon camera with 400,000 pixels", Nature 622, 730-734 (2023-10-25): 400,000 pixels over 4 x 2.5 mm at 5 x 5 um resolution using a thermally coupled row-column readout with no ancillary circuitry in the imaging area; the existence proof that SNSPD channel counts can be multiplexed far beyond one-coax-per-pixel, at the cost of timing resolution [D]

GF-QTS-2026-05.text: GlobalFoundries launched "Quantum Technology Solutions" on 2026-05-21, a business unit for quantum manufacturing across superconducting, trapped-ion, photonic, topological and spin modalities (cryogenic CMOS on FDX, cryo read-out/control ICs, advanced packaging, superconducting interconnects, 3D heterogeneous interconnect); named partners/customers Diraq, Equal1, Google Quantum AI, Microsoft Quantum, NVIDIA, PsiQuantum, Quantinuum, Quantum Motion; states a $375 M CHIPS letter of intent to accelerate the build-out; no fab or wafer size named in the release [C]

PIXEUROPE-2024-11.text: PIXEurope, the European Pilot Line on Advanced Photonic Integrated Circuits, selected by the European Commission and Chips JU 2024-11-24; coordinated by ICFO (Barcelona) with partners in Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Ireland, Italy, Poland, Portugal, Spain, the Netherlands and the UK (imec among them); ~EUR 400 M, 10-year operational phase, billed as the first fully integrated open-access PIC pilot line; co-financed by Spain's Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Generalitat of Catalonia. CONFLICT: trade press headlines the budget as EUR 380 M

TFLN-FUNDING-2024-09.text: Thin-film lithium niobate suppliers raised in 2024-09: HyperLight (Cambridge MA, Harvard spin-off 2018) $37 M Series B led by Summit Partners with Xora Innovation and Foothill Ventures; Lightium (Zurich, CSEM spin-off 2023) $7 M seed led by Vsquared Ventures and Lakestar, foundry service scheduled to launch at the start of 2025 (launch unverified as of 2026-09-03) [P]

ELECGATE-9999-2025-10.text: Hughes, Srinivas, Loschnauer, Knaack, Matt, Ballance, Malinowski, Harty, Sutherland (Oxford Ionics / IonQ), "Trapped-ion two-qubit gates with >99.99% fidelity without ground-state cooling", arXiv:2510.17286 (2025-10-20): "smooth gate" using adiabatic elimination of spin-motion entanglement (ramped gate detuning); estimated two-qubit error 8.4(7)x10^-5 from subspace-leakage randomized benchmarking at Doppler temperature, mean phonon number n-bar = 9.4(3) on the gate mode, no ground-state cooling; error stays <=5x10^-4 at higher temperature; authors claim ~3x better than the previous best 0.9997 (ground-state cooled) and ~100x better than the best ~0.992 without ground-state cooling. Ion species and zone count not stated in the retrievable text; gate duration 225.8 us per the project technology-graph record, not confirmed in the abstract [D]

OXIONICS-ALLELEC-2024-07.text: Loschnauer, Mosca Toba, Hughes, King, Weber, Srinivas, Matt, Nourshargh, Allcock, Ballance, Matthiesen, Malinowski, Harty, "Scalable, high-fidelity all-electronic control of trapped-ion qubits", arXiv:2407.07694 (2024-07-10), PRX Quantum 6, 040313 (2025): seven-zone microfabricated ion trap with shared current-carrying traces and local tuning electrodes, up to 10 qubits controlled; two-qubit 99.97(1)%, single-qubit 99.99916(7)%, no lasers used for gates. This is the widest device on which the electronic (laser-free) gate has been demonstrated as of 2026-09-03 [D]

UQ-DLR-67M-2022-11.text: Universal Quantum (Sussex spin-out, Hensinger) won a EUR 67 M contract from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), announced 2022-11-02: two quantum computers within four years - a single-chip machine and a multi-chip system of up to 100 qubits, modular "jigsaw" connection at moderate cooling temperatures. No delivery, milestone or fidelity result announced as of 2026-09-03 [P]

WISE-ARCH-2023.text: Malinowski, Allcock, Ballance (Oxford Ionics), "How to wire a 1000-qubit trapped ion quantum computer", PRX Quantum 4, 040313 (arXiv:2305.12773, 2023-05-22): WISE = Wiring using Integrated Switching Electronics; a fully connected 1000-qubit trapped-ion machine operated from ~200 signal sources at ~40-2600 quantum gate layers per second, by integrating simple switching electronics into the ion trap chip while complex synthesis stays external; design study, no chip built, no dissipation or DAC count in the abstract [S]

OXFORD-1Q-1E-7-2024-12.text: Smith, Leu, Miyanishi, Gely, Lucas (Oxford), "Single-qubit gates with errors at the 10^-7 level", arXiv:2412.04421 (2024-12-05, rev 2025-05-28): 43Ca+ hyperfine clock qubit in a microfabricated surface-electrode trap with a chip-integrated microwave resonator, room temperature and NO magnetic shielding; minimum error per Clifford 1.5(4)x10^-7 over gate times 4.4-35 us, T2 approximately 70 s, calibration errors suppressed below 10^-8, residual dominated by decoherence, leakage and measurement [D]

QSEA-DLR-2023.text: DLR Quantum Computing Initiative project QSea I: 10-qubit ion-trap demonstrator on eleQtron's MAGIC (magnetic-gradient-induced-coupling microwave control), 2023-03-01 to 2027-02-28, sited at the DLR Innovation Centre Hamburg; eleQtron builds the processor, NXP Semiconductors supplies the control and regulation electronics, ParityQC the architecture/OS; first demonstrator announced live 2024-05-30 (NXP newsroom); contract value not disclosed on the DLR page [G][C]

MSFT-LYNGBY-LAB-2025-11.text: Microsoft opened its largest quantum lab in Lyngby, Denmark on 2025-11-13, described as enabling "the full fabrication of the Majorana chip core in Denmark"; cumulative investment in Danish quantum infrastructure reported above DKK 1 bn (approx. USD 156 M) - the figure is the national total, not Microsoft's own outlay; Microsoft headcount, capex and topological R&D spend undisclosed [P]

MSFT-QUPP-2026-01.text: Microsoft Quantum Pioneers Program 2026 (announced 2026-01-23; applications 2025-11-15 to 2026-01-31, decisions 2026-03-15, 12-month term from 2026-08-01): academic awards up to USD 200,000 per proposal for measurement-based topological quantum computing - simulation, readout and control, QEC, early fault-tolerant experiments, characterisation and verification; no partner institutions named [P]

NOKIA-BELLLABS-TOPO-2026.text: Nokia Bell Labs runs the only non-Microsoft industrial topological-qubit programme: fractional quantum Hall states in GaAs (nu = 5/2 and 7/2), Fabry-Perot interferometry, Robert Willett; Willett et al., Phys. Rev. X 13, 011028 (2023-03-01) report e/4 interference with the predicted even-odd effect and fermion parity stable over hours [D]. Trade press adds ~15 x 15 um devices, an end-2025 Pauli-X control result (no publication found as of 2026-09-03) and an end-2026 target for a topological qubit in superposition [P]

INFINEON-IONTRAP-FAB-2026.text: Infineon Technologies operates a dedicated QPU platform at Villach (AT) producing ion traps on 6- to 12-inch wafers with anodic wafer bonding; Generation-3 traps add out-of-plane electrodes claimed to raise ion confinement ~10x versus a plain surface trap. Named users: eleQtron (three progressively improved trap generations), Oxford Ionics (fully integrated QPUs, "hundreds of qubits within five years"), University of Innsbruck (parallel shuttling), ETH Zurich TIQI (Gen-3 test). Separate Infineon-Quantinuum partnership on next-generation traps announced 2024-11-19, no financial terms. Infineon is thus the merchant trap fab for IonQ/Oxford Ionics, eleQtron and Universal Quantum simultaneously, while Honeywell fabricates Quantinuum's traps in-house [C][P]

AQT-LRZ-9.8M-2023-12.text: AQT (Alpine Quantum Technologies, Innsbruck) delivered a 20-qubit trapped-ion quantum computer to the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre (LRZ) in cooperation with Munich Quantum Valley for approximately EUR 9.8 M, announced 2023-12-05; funded by the Bavarian State Ministries StMWK and StMWi under the Hightech Agenda Bavaria; system supplied as ion trap plus laser and camera unit and control electronics in two 19-inch racks. Implies roughly EUR 0.5 M per qubit for a turnkey room-temperature installation - the only publicly quotable trapped-ion unit price found as of 2026-09-03 [C]

ION-SUPPLYCHAIN-2026.text: Trapped-ion supply chain concentration as of 2026-09-03 (secondary analysis): lasers - TOPTICA Photonics (Munich, >EUR 140 M revenue, ~600 staff) supplies most major ion experiments, UV wavelengths (369 nm for Yb+) the constrained part; alternatives MOGLabs, Menlo Systems, Coherent, NKT, Thorlabs. Modulators: Gooch & Housego, AA Opto-Electronic. Trap fab: Infineon Villach (merchant) and Honeywell (captive, Quantinuum); Sandia research-only. UHV: Pfeiffer, Edwards, Agilent, Kurt J. Lesker, VACOM, SAES - no concentration. Detectors for photonic interconnect: Single Quantum, Photon Spot, ID Quantique (IonQ-owned). Two genuine single points of failure: UV laser supply and Infineon's fab [P]

QUIX-SERIESA-2025-07.text: QuiX Quantum (Enschede NL) closed a EUR 15 M Series A announced 2025-07-10, co-led by Invest-NL and the EIC Fund with PhotonVentures, Oost NL and FORWARD.one; roadmap: first-generation universal photonic quantum computer in 2026 (already sold and contracted for delivery), next generation with error correction 2027; the 8-qubit "Carina" core hardware platform was delivered to DLR QCI 2026-07, commissioning pending; company names fast feed-forward electronics and single-photon sources as the two problems the 2026 system must solve [C]

SPARROW-SERIESA-2025-04.text: Sparrow Quantum (Copenhagen DK), the only merchant vendor of deterministic quantum-dot single-photon source chips as of 2026-09-03: EUR 21.5 M (USD 24 M) Series A announced 2025-04-10, lead investor not disclosed in the retrievable release [P]; selected 2026-06-19 by the EuroHPC JU Quantum Grand Challenge (1 of 13 from 30 proposals, the only Danish company) for project EU-SCALE, EUR 300,000, grant agreement in preparation [P]. Device data (arXiv:2511.23232): S1 system efficiency 55.3%, 26.2 MHz detected rate at 80 MHz pump, purity 98.8%; S3 raw HOM visibility 97.1 +/- 0.1% and purity 99.9 +/- 0.1%; typical production devices 20-35% system efficiency versus the 71.2% USTC laboratory record

PSIQ-BRISBANE-940M.text: PsiQuantum Brisbane: A$940 M joint commitment from the Australian federal and Queensland governments (2024-04; instrument mix equity/loan/grant not restated in the source); site moved from Brisbane Airport Industrial Park to Moreton Bay Central to avoid a Major Development Plan consultation, formal groundbreaking June 2026, stated target a commercially useful quantum computer by end-2027; interim CEO Victor Peng cited the new site's infrastructure and scalability [P]

INFLEQTION-Q2-2026-08.text: Infleqtion (NYSE: INFQ) Q2 2026 results, released 2026-08-12: revenue USD 12.6 M, +116% year on year and stated as 100% organic and entirely from quantum; H1 2026 revenue USD 22.094 M (H1 2025 USD 14.140 M); FY2026 guidance raised to approximately USD 43 M; Q2 net loss USD 25.5 M, H1 net loss USD 55.7 M; USD 582 M cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and available-for-sale securities at 2026-06-30, no debt; reaffirms 30 logical qubits in 2026 and a neutral-atom system at Illinois Quantum & Microelectronics Park in 2027 scaling beyond 50 logical qubits; selected for three DoE Genesis Mission projects [G]

TSINGHUA-METASURFACE-2026-06.text: Wang, Zhang et al. (Tsinghua University and Qosmos, Beijing), arXiv:2606.02715 (2026-06-01): 11,022 individual 87Rb atoms trapped in an 18,225-site (135x135) tweezer array generated by a 19.8 mm silicon-nitride metasurface placed 2.5 mm outside the vacuum cell (~1.5 cm working distance), replacing the microscope objective; 33 W incident at 850 nm, 12.2 W effective trapping power (~0.67 mW per site), 780 nm detection; average filling fraction 60.5% pre-rearrangement; NO gates, no coherence measurement; vacuum lifetime not stated [D]

PASQAL-PIC-2026-08.text: Pasqal newsroom 2026-08-10: four individual rubidium atoms trapped by light delivered from a silicon-nitride photonic integrated circuit (4 optical traps from one chip), atom lifetime approximately 27.5 s, performance stated as in line with the company's bulk-optics systems; technology from Aeponyx, acquired by Pasqal less than 18 months earlier; company claims a potential 50x reduction in optical footprint and a long-term target of >10,000 atoms / 100 logical qubits; laser wavelengths not disclosed [C]

IBM-HRL-CLOSED-2026-08.text: IBM completed its acquisition of HRL Laboratories on 2026-08-26 (announced 2026-07-23); terms undisclosed; IBM gains silicon-spin qubits, quantum sensing, quantum materials, cryogenics, control electronics, packaging and interconnect; former owners Boeing and General Motors remain application partners; IBM names possible collaboration with Anderon, its quantum wafer foundry; no spin milestone placed on the Starling (2029) or Blue Jay (mid-2030s) roadmap [C]

SI28-SUPPLY-2026.text: Enriched silicon-28 supply as of 2026-09-03: ASP Isotopes commenced commercial production at its second Pretoria (ZA) aerodynamic-separation facility 2025-03-27 with two undisclosed US customers (a semiconductor company and an industrial gas company), first shipments guided to Q2 2025 [C]; US DOE Office of Isotope R&D and Production announced 2026-07-16 that ORNL (electromagnetic separation) and PNNL (thermal diffusion) now produce silane at 99.9999% Si-28 and germane with Ge-73 below 1 ppm, claimed "at least 100x" more isotopically depleted than any commercial material, restoring a US capability lost when the wartime calutrons were decommissioned in 1998; quantities and funding not disclosed [G]

SEMIQON-2026.text: SemiQon (VTT Technical Research Centre spin-out, founded 2023, Otaniemi/Espoo FI; cryo-CMOS control and readout chips fabricated in-house): EUR 17.5 M announced 2025-02-24 (EUR 15 M equity + EUR 2.5 M European Innovation Council grant) [P]; strategic investment from PostScriptum (Peter Sarlin) announced 2026-07-03, amount undisclosed; entered commercial phase spring 2026, components stated to be deployed in working quantum systems [P]

QXLABS-QECCT-2026-07.text: Quantum X Labs (Nasdaq: QXL) benchmarked its transformer decoder QECCT against classical MWPM using NVIDIA CUDA-Q QEC libraries in an AWS cloud environment, with Quantum Machines/IQCC and Google surface-code geometry as reference; QECCT reported to outperform MWPM in selected simulated regimes, no quantitative figure or peer review disclosed

MICROBLOSSOM-2026.text: Yue Wu (Yale), "micro-blossom": FPGA-accelerated exact MWPM decoder on an AMD/Xilinx VMK180 board (152k LUTs), cuts decode latency from 5.1 microseconds (CPU) to 367 nanoseconds (14x), supports 1M measurement rounds/second, targets up to 110 logical qubits; MIT-licensed GitHub repo, no peer-reviewed paper as of 2026-09-03 ("paper coming soon")

GOOGLE-COLORBLOG-2025-06.text: Google Research blog "A colorful quantum future" (2025-06-23): colour code logical Hadamard ~20 ns vs ~1,000x longer via surface-code lattice surgery, two-qubit gate fidelity 86-91%, magic-state injection 99% fidelity; states colour code will be a "workhorse configuration" alongside the surface code in Google's large-scale roadmap

PATSNAP-QEC-LANDSCAPE-2026-04.text: PatSnap Insights "Quantum error correction patent landscape 2026" (2026-04-22): 12 tracked QEC patents - Google 6 (JP/KR/EP), IBM 4 (EP/IL/SG), Tencent 2 (KR/JP); no colour-code-specific patent cluster identified; Quantinuum's 2021 [[7,1,3]] colour-code demo treated as literature reference, not IP

MUNICH-VTT-CRYOLINK-2025.text: Yam, Renger, Gandorfer et al. (MCQST/TU Munich, VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland), "Cryogenic microwave link for quantum local area networks", npj Quantum Information 11, 87 (2025-05-31): squeezed-microwave-state link between two separate dilution cryostats over 6.6 m, base temperature 52 mK at channel center, squeezing 2.10±0.02 dB, negativity 0.501±0.011, entanglement preserved to channel-center temperatures up to 1 K, cable attenuation 1.01 dB/km at 5.65 GHz [D]

ULVAC-IBM-REFRIG-2025.text: ULVAC, Inc./ULVAC Cryogenics announced 2025-03-21 a next-generation dilution refrigerator for quantum computing developed with IBM input, targeting the ~10 mK level, tested at IBM Poughkeepsie, industry deployment targeted "early 2026"; explicitly framed as adding a domestic Japanese third source alongside Bluefors and Oxford Instruments [C]

IBM-AMD-RELAYBP-FPGA-2025.text: Trade press (HPCwire, 2025-10-28) reports IBM demonstrating its Relay-BP gross-code decoder on AMD FPGAs, framed as lower-cost than prior decoder hardware; full pricing and partnership terms not independently confirmed after a fetch failure (redirect error) [P]

NVQLINK-QUANTINUUM-2025-11.text: NVIDIA NVQLink launched 2025-11-17 with Quantinuum as the first named QPU partner: nv-qldpc-decoder runs on a GH200 Grace Hopper superchip against Quantinuum's 98-qubit Helios, RoCE round trip 3.84 µs mean (0.035 µs SD), BP-OSD median decode 67 µs, 5.4× logical-error-rate improvement; RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q used in a separate networking demonstration; Quantinuum states future processors will also deploy NVQLink [C]

KYOTO-FASTIMG-2026-08.text: Yokoyama, Kashimoto, Shibata et al. (Kyoto University, with Yaqumo Inc.), arXiv:2605.24175v2 (2026-08-24): 17.6 microsecond fluorescence imaging of 174-Yb atoms on an Andor iXon-Ultra897 EMCCD (399 nm probe, NA-0.6 objective), 99.89(5)% discrimination, 98.80(44)% survival, heating rate ~half of prior incoherent excitation schemes

USTC-FASTREADOUT-2026-08.text: Zeng, You, ... Pan et al. (USTC), "Fast Nondestructive Readout for High-Clock-Rate Atom Array Quantum Processor", arXiv:2608.17189 (2026-08-17): 100-qubit reconfigurable atom array, 15 microsecond average probe duration, discrimination infidelity 4.1e-5, atom loss 2.1e-4, 1.7 kHz clock rate sustained over 120 consecutive rounds (~7x prior record) via real-time site-resolved adaptive protection plus continuous photon counting; atom species not stated in the retrievable abstract

AQT-LYNX-QV-2026-05.text: AQT (Alpine Quantum Technologies) "LYNX" ion-trap module sets a quantum-volume record of 32,768 (announced 2026-05-05); first units scheduled for select strategic partners in Q4 2026 with wider commercial availability following; junction vs linear-only architecture and transport/gate times not disclosed in the release [C]

QART-SERIES-DETAIL-2026-04.text: Quantum Art (Israel) Series A extended to $140 M total (2026-04-27), up from a $100 M close in 2025-12; lead investor Bedford Ridge Capital, with Hudson Bay Capital, Poalim Equity, LIP Ventures, Wolverine Global Ventures and IDA Ventures; funds target the 1,000-qubit "Perspective" multi-core 2D trapped-ion system and optical scaling technology [C]

GOOGLE-GOLETA-2026-08.text: Google acquired an adjoining 83,356 sq ft campus (147/153 Castilian Drive) in Goleta near its Santa Barbara Quantum AI lab (301 Mentor Drive), expanding its local footprint to ~300,000 sq ft; purpose not stated as fab-specific in the source

OQC-WAFERPKG-2026-02.text: OQC wafer-scale superconducting-qubit package: >500 qubits on one 3-inch die, readout fidelity 97.5% median (n=54 sampled), T1/T2e ~100 µs median (~100 sampled), operating temperature 36 mK median — sub-sampled, not a full-wafer census

AFT-PAPER-2024-06.text: Zhou, Zhao, Cain, Bluvstein, Maskara, Duckering, Hu, Wang, Kubica, Lukin, "Low-Overhead Transversal Fault Tolerance for Universal Quantum Computation," arXiv:2406.17653 (2024-06): introduces "algorithmic fault tolerance" — transversal (block-to-block) logical gates plus correlated decoding across the full syndrome history, replacing O(d) syndrome-extraction rounds per logical gate with a constant number; claims >10x space-time cost reduction vs standard lattice surgery; simulation/theory only, no hardware demonstration of the combined scheme as of 2026-09-03 [D][S]

GOOGLE-ATOMS-STRUCTURE-2026-03.text: Google Quantum AI neutral-atom hardware track (announced 2026-03-24): led by Adam Kaufman, recruited from NIST/JILA (CU Boulder), who retains his JILA Fellowship and academic post; based in Boulder, CO; three declared pillars — QEC adapted for neutral-atom connectivity, modelling/simulation on Google compute, and experimental hardware development; positioned as complementary to, not a replacement for, Google's superconducting roadmap; no budget, headcount or commercial date disclosed [C]

AOD-SUPPLY-2026.text: Named crossed-AOD suppliers for neutral-atom tweezer transport: AA Opto-Electronic (DTSX-400 model, used in Harvard/MIT/QuEra's 448-atom zoned architecture, alongside Hamamatsu SLM/camera, Spectrum Instrumentation AWGs, Rohde & Schwarz microwave source) and Gooch & Housego (G&H, cited in Nature papers reporting 3,000- and 6,100-qubit arrays); neither vendor found public or separately funded

GOOGLE-ATOMS-KAUFMAN-2026-03.text: Google's neutral-atom hardware track (led by Adam Kaufman, ex-NIST/JILA) collaborates with QuEra, CU Boulder, JILA, NIST Boulder and Elevate Quantum; three pillars: QEC, modeling/simulation, experimental hardware; framed as complementary to superconducting, not a replacement

CHIP-SPS-ATOM-2026-08.text: Hu, Zhang, Zou et al., "A scalable chip-integrated single-photon source array based on 50 individually addressable neutral atoms," arXiv:2608.15637 (2026-08-16): 50-channel glass-waveguide fan-out converting a 5 micron optical-tweezer-array pitch to a commercial fiber-array pitch, Rb-87 atoms, average nearest-neighbour cross-talk 0.4%, uniform insertion loss 2.9 dB across 50 channels; institutional affiliation not stated in the retrievable abstract text [D]

PASQAL-AEPONYX-DETAIL-2026-08.text: Pasqal's August 2026 on-chip qubit-control announcement states its silicon-nitride PIC uses photonics expertise from Aeponyx, acquired by Pasqal "less than 18 months" before the 2026-08-10 release (implying acquisition around early-to-mid 2025, exact date/price undisclosed in any source found); no foundry partner (imec, GlobalFoundries etc.) is named for the chip; roadmap target ">10,000 atoms and 100 logical qubits" carries no date [C]

IONQ-PHOTONIC-INTERCONNECT-2026-04.text: IonQ announced its first photonic-interconnect milestone, networking two separate trapped-ion quantum systems via entanglement, with AFRL as a named partner (Case AFRL-2026-1742); no rate, fidelity or distance disclosed for the link itself; CEO framed it as foundational toward a "quantum internet"

OXFORD-DISTRIBUTEDQC-2025-02.text: Oxford distributed quantum computing across an optical network (Main, Drmota et al., Nature 638, 383): remote Bell-pair fidelity 96.89(8)% at ~9.7 s⁻¹ (103 ms/attempt), teleported CZ 86.2(9)%, distributed iSWAP 70(2)%, distributed SWAP 64(2)%, distributed Grover success 71(1)%

ION-SEIDELIN-2006.text: Seidelin, Chiaverini et al. (NIST), first microfabricated surface-electrode ion trap: ²⁴Mg⁺ held ~40 µm above planar gold electrodes, motional heating rate measured directly, establishing the anomalous-heating floor that scales with proximity to the electrode surface

IONQ-SKYWATER-FAB-2026.text: IonQ's completed-acquisition release for SkyWater Technology (2026-07-31) names facilities in Minnesota, Florida and Texas and states the deal secures "chip design, fabrication, and packaging" for a "fully scalable supply chain domestically," unlocking a "semiconductor-based approach" to building future ion-trap/control chips; no wafer size, process node, or ion-trap-specific capacity disclosed [C]

GTC-GMON-2014.text: Chen, Neill, Roushan, Leung, Fang, Barends, Kelly, Campbell, Chen, Chiaro, Dunsworth, Jeffrey, Megrant, Mutus, O'Malley, Quintana, Sank, Vainsencher, Wenner, White, Cleland, Martinis (Google/UCSB), "Qubit Architecture with High-Coherence and Fast Tunable Coupling" (the "gmon" coupler), arXiv:1402.7367, Phys. Rev. Lett. 113, 220502 (2014): tunable coupling settable to zero at nanosecond resolution alongside high qubit coherence — the origin paper for flux-tunable-coupler CZ/iSWAP gates

IBM-TCOUPLER-PATENT-2023.text: IBM, US Patent 11,727,297 B2, "Tunable quantum coupler facilitating a quantum gate between qubits" (Stehlik, Underwood, Zajac, Steffen; filed 2020-06-24, granted 2023-08-15): coupler paired with a capacitor providing an opposite-sign second coupling path to cancel unwanted coherent rotation and improve 2Q gate fidelity [P]

SILENTWAVES-TWPA-2026.text: Silent Waves (Grenoble, France): commercial TWPA maker, product line Argo (flagship readout TWPA), Carthago (tunable TWPA) and Zephyr (integrated TWPA+pump-coupler, launched 2026-03-13); named customers Rigetti, Alice & Bob, Qilimanjaro Quantum Computing, QphoX and CEA; 2025 Nature Electronics paper on a "travelling-wave parametric amplifier isolator"; BPI France/CNRS Innovation (RISE) listed as partners [C]

QUANTUMCORE-TWPA-2026.text: QuantumCore Inc. (CSE: QNCR, Canada): superconducting TWPA developer; public listing 2026-04-14; $1.7 M non-dilutive NSERC Alliance Quantum grant announced 2026-04-25 with IQC/U. Waterloo (CTO Christopher Wilson); $10.7 M total funding to date, 7 employees, dedicated Waterloo lab [C][G]

CRYOZIP-2026-06.text: "CryoZip": Tao, Knapen, Mack, Saligane et al. (Univ. Michigan + Brown Univ.), arXiv:2606.30805 (2026-06-29): 22 nm FDSOI cryogenic (4 K) syndrome compressor, up to 48x compression ratio alone; combined with a predecoder (Pinball-class), up to 14,238x syndrome-bandwidth reduction and up to 42x system energy saving; design/synthesis study, not fabricated [S]

FROSTBYTE-2026-05.text: FrostByte (TU Delft/QuTech spin-off, Netherlands): EUR 1.3 M (USD 1.5 M) pre-seed, announced 2026-05-12, led by UNIIQ, Paeonia Group, InnovationQuarter, Graduate Ventures + one angel; first product a family of cryogenic RF switches operating to millikelvin, positioned as cold-located qubit-control electronics [C]

QUTECH-NV-CAVITY-2026-01.text: Fischer et al. (QuTech/Delft), "cavity-enhanced NV photon collection," Nature Communications, 2026-01-15: fibre-based Fabry-Perot microcavity around a single NV centre raises resonant photon-collection probability roughly 10x, ~0.05% to ~0.5%; spin coherence >100 us under echo retained [D]

QUTECH-NV-TELEPORT-CNOT-2026-05.text: Hanson et al. (QuTech/Delft), "Unconditionally teleported quantum gates between remote solid-state qubit registers," Nature Communications, 2026-05-26: unconditional (no post-selection) CNOT between NV-centre qubit registers in two separate cryostats via real-time feed-forward; 4-qubit GHZ fidelity 64(4)%, CNOT-mediated entangled-state fidelity 63(4)%. NOTE: technology-graph record ic_spinphoton.json attributes a similar inter-cryostat teleported-CNOT claim to T-centre technology; this is the only matching 2026 result located and it is NV-based, not T-centre — flag as possible mis-attribution [D]

QUTECH-BASEBAND-2025-07.text: Unseld, Undseth, Raymenants et al. (QuTech/Delft), "Baseband control of single-electron silicon spin qubits in two dimensions," Nature Communications, 2025-07-01: exclusively baseband (no microwave) control via voltage pulses exploiting an on-chip micromagnet's stray-field gradient for diabatic spin hopping between dots; 2x2 quantum-dot array (4-qubit processor); hopping-gate fidelity lower bound 99.50(6)%, Hahn-echo T2 up to ~49 us (nearly double high-field EDSR operation) [D]

SEEQC-ALLEGRO-2026-07.text: SEEQC filed Form S-1 for Nasdaq listing (2026-07-02) via a parallel SPAC business-combination agreement with Allegro Merger Corp. (Form S-4): combined entity valued ~$1 B, $65 M PIPE facility; Cantor and BTIG lead underwriters; SEEQC's SFQ chips report gate fidelities >99.9% at nanowatt-scale power; IBM and NVIDIA named as active collaboration pipelines [C]

DWAVE-FLUXDAC-2026-01.text: D-Wave whitepaper 14-1090A-A (2026-01-23), "Digital Control of High-Coherence Fluxonium Qubits": flip-chip-bonded SFQ on-chip flux-DAC (Φ-DAC) controlling a single fluxonium, ~7 um vacuum gap between qubit chip and multilayer control chip, cooled to T=10 mK; T1~200 us, T2*~20 us, "no resolvable increase in decoherence" from the Φ-DAC; D-Wave's existing annealers use ~300 bias lines to control several-thousand flux qubits and tens-of-thousands of couplers [D]

SANDIA-QTM-CRADA-2026-05.text: Sandia National Laboratories and Quantinuum renewed a four-year Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA), reported 2026-08-27 as renewed in May 2026: Sandia's MESA complex supplies integrated-photonics chips for trapped-ion control, framed as improving scalability and reducing energy cost of laser delivery to ions [G]

IONQ-SANDIA-MOU-2026-08.text: IonQ and Sandia National Laboratories signed an MOU (2026-08-04) for "accelerated co-design of quantum information science technologies" for US national-security applications; IonQ names silicon photonics and Sandia's trapped-ion fabrication expertise as the two areas that most determine scaling speed and interconnect quality; no funding amount disclosed [C]

DELFT-BLUEFORS-CRIOFLEX-2025-11.text: Delft Circuits' Cri/oFlex flexible cryogenic RF cabling integrated into Bluefors dilution refrigerators (announced 2025-11-10): 8 channels/flex, up to 50% more channels per side-loading port, 1,536 lines achievable in one XLDsl configuration; vendor roadmap cites 150+ qubits today, 40,000+ by 2029 [C]

ZI-ZQCS-2026-03.text: Zurich Instruments (Rohde & Schwarz) launched the ZQCS quantum control platform (2026-03-09): >1,000 channels/rack, µs-scale feedback, targets "several thousand qubits" with five-nines-and-beyond gate fidelities; deployed on Fujitsu/RIKEN's 256-qubit system; first installations running QEC experiments [C]

SPARROW-SUBTHRESHOLD-2026-06.text: Löbl, Pettersson, Dragašević, Chen, Sandberg (Sparrow Quantum / Center for Hybrid Quantum Networks), "The subthreshold issue of fusion-based quantum computing," arXiv:2606.28490 (2026-06-26): fusion failure imposes a noise floor persisting even at zero physical loss, so all-linear-optics 6-ring designs need very large code distance/overhead to reach ~10⁻¹⁰ logical error rates; hybrid quantum-emitter fusion (FFCC RUS) gives a 7.0-7.3% loss threshold vs an unencoded 6-ring's 0.38-0.82% (static bias)/0.78% (random bias), reducing overhead by orders of magnitude versus all-linear-optics [S]

UQ-MATTERLINK-2023-02.text: Akhtar, Bonus, Lebrun-Gallagher, Johnson, Siegele-Brown, Hong, Hile, Kulmiya, Weidt, Hensinger (Universal Quantum), "A high-fidelity quantum matter-link between ion-trap microchip modules", Nature Communications 14, 531 (2023-02-08): ions physically transported between two separate ion-trap microchip modules across a 10(1) um inter-module gap at 2,424 transfers/s, 1.66 m/s average, infidelity from ion loss during transport below 7x10^-8, no measurable loss of qubit coherence over 100 links (T2* 540(30) ms vs 560(40) ms stationary), 174Yb+/171Yb+. NIST-FASTTRANSPORT-2012.text: Bowler, Gaebler, Lin, Tan, Hanneke, Jost, Home, Leibfried, Wineland (NIST), "Coherent diabatic ion transport and separation in a multizone trap array", Phys. Rev. Lett. 109, 080502 (arXiv:1206.0780, 2012-06-04): 9Be+ moved 370 um in 8 us (16 periods of a 2 MHz well) with motional excitation peaking at 1.6 quanta and returning to 0.2 quanta by waveform design; chains of up to 9 ions separated into two wells; two-ion separation in 55 us leaving ~2 quanta per ion. Establishes that the hop itself is microsecond-scale, so millisecond QCCD layer times come from split/merge, re-ordering and re-cooling, not from transport speed [D]

RELAYBP-ORIGIN-2025-06.text: Relay-BP was introduced by Mueller, Alexander, Beverland, Buehler, Johnson, Maurer, Vandeth (IBM), "Improved belief propagation is sufficient for real-time decoding of quantum memory", arXiv:2506.01779 (2025-06-02, rev. 2025-08-22) — NOT in the later FPGA paper arXiv:2510.21600, which is a different IBM author set. Mechanism: per-node disordered memory strengths that must include negative values ("indispensable"), plus chained relay legs; reported to significantly outperform BP+OSD+CS-10 on bivariate-bicycle codes and to be comparable to min-weight matching on surface codes; abstract gives no numeric factor and no latency [D]

RELAYBP-LATENCY-CONFLICT.text: Conflict on the Relay-BP FPGA timing figure: arXiv:2510.21600's abstract states a belief-propagation iteration time of 24 ns and an "average per cycle decoding time under 1 microsecond" for physical error probabilities below 3e-3, whereas the graph/technology-graph record row records "480 ns per 12-cycle window" (~25x apart). The abstract also states no FPGA part, no LUT/memory usage, no arithmetic precision and no LER improvement factor; the "~100x lower LER than BP-OSD" attributed to Relay-BP appears in neither abstract [D]

ALTERA-SILVERLAKE-2025.text: Intel agreed to sell 51% of Altera to Silver Lake at an $8.75 B enterprise valuation (announced 2025-04-14), receiving approximately $4.46 B and retaining 49%; Altera becomes an independent FPGA company. This leaves the merchant high-end FPGA market — the substrate for every published real-time QEC decoder (Riverlane LCD on Xilinx VU19P, micro-blossom on VMK180, Shenzhen NN decoder on Kintex-7, IBM Relay-BP reported on AMD) — as an AMD/Altera duopoly with one side under private-equity control [G]

MICROBLOSSOM-ASPLOS-2025.text: Wu, Liyanage, Zhong (Yale), "Micro Blossom: Accelerated Minimum-Weight Perfect Matching Decoding for Quantum Error Correction", ASPLOS 2025 (arXiv:2502.14787, 2025-02-20): exact MWPM decoding in FPGA hardware with O(d^3) parallel processing units, average latency 0.8 us at d=13 and p=0.1% at a 62 MHz clock, 8x shorter than the best previously reported MWPM latency; worst-case complexity cut from O(d^12) to O(d^9), average from O(p d^3 + 1) to O(p^2 d^2 + 1). CORRECTS fact record key MICROBLOSSOM-2026, which recorded the project as unpublished ("paper coming soon"); the repository's 367 ns / 1M-rounds-per-second figures appear in no paper and carry no stated code distance [D]

WILLOW-RTDECODER-2024.text: Google Quantum AI, "Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold" (Nature 638, 920; arXiv:2408.13687): the real-time decoder for the distance-5 10^6-cycle run is a specialised, parallelised version of the Sparse Blossom algorithm ("optimized to quickly resolve local configurations of errors common in surface code decoding"), 63 us mean latency, not stock PyMatching; the paper reports Lambda = 2.14 +/- 0.02 with the neural-network decoder against Lambda = 2.04 +/- 0.02 with ensembled matching synthesis — the measured accuracy gap between matching and a neural decoder on identical syndromes [D]
