AFT-RESOURCE-ISCA-2025.text: Zhou, Duckering, Zhao, Bluvstein, Cain, Kubica, Wang, Lukin, "Resource Analysis of Low-Overhead Transversal Architectures for Reconfigurable Atom Arrays", ISCA 2025 (arXiv:2505.15907, 2025-05-21; doi 10.1145/3695053.3731039): RSA-2048 factoring with 19 million qubits in 5.6 days at a 1 ms QEC cycle, close to 50x speed-up over comparable estimates with no additional space overhead; building blocks are magic-state factories, quantum arithmetic units and quantum look-up tables built from transversal operations. Physical error rate and code distance not stated in the abstract [S]

SHOR-10K-ATOMS-2026-03.text: Cain, Xu, King, Picard, Levine, Endres, Preskill, Huang, Bluvstein, "Shor's algorithm is possible with as few as 10,000 reconfigurable atomic qubits" (arXiv:2603.28627, 2026-03-30): minimum 10,000 reconfigurable atomic qubits for a cryptographically relevant run, 26,000 for better time efficiency; P-256 elliptic-curve discrete logarithms "could be just a few days", RSA-2048 factoring "one to two orders of magnitude longer" than P-256. NOTE: this is NOT an RSA-2048-in-days estimate - the 19 M-qubit / 5.6-day figure of AFT-RESOURCE-ISCA-2025 is the fast end of the same space-time trade curve; citing "RSA-2048 with 10,000 atoms" misstates both papers [S]

GOOGLE-COLORCODE-2024-12.text: Lacroix, Bourassa, Heras, Zhang et al. (Google Quantum AI, 300 authors), "Scaling and logic in the colour code on a superconducting quantum processor", arXiv:2412.14256 (2024-12-18), Nature 645, 614-619 (2025): error-suppression factor Lambda_3/5 = 1.56(4); transversal Clifford gates add error 0.0027(3); magic-state injection fidelity above 99% only with post-selection retaining about 75% of runs; lattice-surgery teleported-state fidelities 86.5(1)% to 90.7(1)%. NOTE: Google's 2025-06-23 blog presents that 86-91% range as "two-qubit gate fidelity" (fact record key GOOGLE-COLORBLOG-2025-06) where the paper reports teleported-state fidelities - same numbers, different quantity, unreconciled [D]

COLORCODE-HOOKFREE-2026-03.text: "Color code off-the-hook: avoiding hook errors with a single auxiliary per plaquette", arXiv:2603.28852 (2026-03): syndrome-extraction circuit for the 2D colour code using one auxiliary qubit per plaquette that avoids all malign hook errors in the bulk, with no single boundary hook error reducing the distance; states it outperforms the previous state of the art in Monte Carlo simulation but the abstract gives no threshold or logical-error figure, and authors/institutions could not be resolved from the arXiv abstract page [S]

COLORCODE-PLANAR-NONCLIFF-2025.text: "Planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code", arXiv:2505.05175, accepted in PRX Quantum (doi 10.1103/p7c9-x1m9): planar circuit construction for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates directly on the 2D colour code, an alternative to magic-state distillation; quantitative overhead claims could not be extracted from the fetched abstract page as of 2026-09-04 [S]

USTC-50ATOM-ARRAY-2026-08.text: Hu, Zhang, Ma, Zhang, Chen, Zhu, Fan, Zhang, Wang, Li, Ren, Guo, Zou, "A scalable chip-integrated single-photon source array based on 50 individually addressable neutral atoms", arXiv:2608.15637 (2026-08-16): 50 individually addressed 87Rb atoms interfaced through a glass waveguide chip, average nearest-neighbour cross-talk 0.4%, uniform insertion loss 2.9 dB, single-photon purity g2(0) = 0.29, 93% fill fraction in 24-atom subarrays, atom-loss repair at 118 Hz, and a 784-channel waveguide chip fabricated. This is an addressing and photon-collection interface, not a chip-generated trap; no gate or trap lifetime is reported. Affiliation inferred as USTC from the author list, not stated on the abstract page [D]

UCHICAGO-ATOMPIC-2024-07.text: Menon, Glachman, Pompili, Dibos, Bernien (Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, University of Chicago), "An integrated atom array-nanophotonic chip platform with background-free imaging", Nature Communications 15, 6156 (2024-07-22): up to 64 optical tweezers over more than 100 nanophotonic cavities on a millimetre-scale 330 nm silicon-nitride-on-silicon chip, ~99.2% imaging fidelity from a multichromatic two-photon excitation scheme, atoms held a few hundred nanometres above the dielectric surface. IMPORTANT: the tweezers are free-space, NOT chip-generated - this is atom-to-photonics coupling, and the sub-micron atom-surface distance rules out Rydberg-gate operation in that geometry [D]

USTC-FASTREADOUT-DETAIL-2026-08.text: Refinement of USTC-FASTREADOUT-2026-08 (arXiv:2608.17189): the 15 microsecond figure is an AVERAGE probe time under adaptive stopping, and the 1.7 kHz / 120-consecutive-round demonstration applied real-time site-resolved adaptive protection to a 25-site subarray of the 100-qubit array, not to the full array; state decoding uses continuous photon counting with a dynamic feed-forward framework at sub-microsecond latency. Atom species, transition, detector type and collection NA are not stated in the retrievable abstract as of 2026-09-04 [D]

QM-NEUTRAL-READOUT-2026-06.text: Quantum Machines, "Classically accelerated readout for neutral atoms" (2026-06): full readout chain on a 10x10 atom array measured at 460 microseconds total - 442 us camera-to-server transfer, 21-85 us processing on 1-24 CPU cores, 2 us OPNIC streaming - at 99.9% per-site fidelity, using a Teledyne Kinetix camera. The frame transfer, not the optical exposure, is the dominant readout term once fast imaging (15-17.6 us) is available; self-reported, not independently audited [C]

SKYT-FY2025-REV.text: SkyWater Technology FY2025 results (fiscal year ended 2025-12-28, released 2026-02-26): revenue $442.1 M (legacy ATS development $212.5 M, legacy wafer services $25.2 M, SkyWater Texas/Fab 25 wafer services $175.6 M, tools $28.9 M), GAAP gross margin 19.7%; the company ended 2025 with eight commercial ATS engagements with quantum-computing companies and quantum-related ATS revenue up over 30% YoY; IonQ's offer of $35.00 per share in cash and stock (announced 2026-01-26) is disclosed as a subsequent event [G]

ION-TRAP-HEATING-FLOOR.text: Anomalous-heating floor of surface-electrode ion traps: electric-field noise measured over 30-3000 um ion-surface distance scales roughly as d^-4 with wide inter-trap spread (Brownnutt, Kumph, Rabl, Blatt, Rev. Mod. Phys. 87, 1419, arXiv:1409.6572); cooling electroplated-gold traps to 6 K suppressed heating by about seven orders of magnitude, two orders below comparable room-temperature traps (Labaziewicz et al., PRL 100, 013001, arXiv:0706.3763); in-situ argon-ion-beam bombardment cut field noise 100-fold on an already-clean trap (Hite et al., PRL 109, 103001, arXiv:1112.5419) - i.e. the floor is surface adsorbate chemistry, not lithography [D]

QECOOL-2021-03.text: arXiv:2103.14209 is Ueno, Kondo, Tanaka, Suzuki, Tabuchi, "QECOOL: On-Line Quantum Error Correction with a Superconducting Decoder for Surface Code" (DAC 2021, 2021-03-25) — an SFQ SUPERCONDUCTING decoder, NOT cryo-CMOS: ~2.78 uW at a 2 GHz clock, 1.0% accuracy threshold, code distances 5-13, simulation only. The "<= 20 ns latency" figure often bundled with it belongs to a different paper, NISQ+ (Holmes, Jokar, Pasandi, Ding, Pedram, Chong, ISCA 2020, arXiv:2004.04794), which reports ~20 ns worst-case decode at the largest distance studied, one SFQ module per physical qubit and a 5% accuracy threshold [S]

CRYO-DECODER-SUPPLY-2026.text: Both published cryogenic-decoder designs (Pinball arXiv:2512.09807, CryoZip arXiv:2606.30805) are built on a 4 K-characterised 22 nm FDSOI PDK supplied by Semiwise Ltd (UK) — a single small vendor gating the cryo-CMOS design path — and are funded by US DOE Office of Science ARQC award DE-SC0025633 (amount not disclosed in either paper) with NERSC compute and Michigan's Quantum Research Institute. CORRECTS attribution: Pinball's author list is entirely University of Michigan; only Saligane is at Brown University, on CryoZip. Pinball adds: under a 1.5 W budget at 4 K the predecoder supports up to 2,668 logical qubits at d=21, 22.2x typical power reduction from peak via DVFS, 67.4x energy saving including interface overheads [S]

SEEQC-S4-TERMS-2026-05.text: SEEQC / Allegro Merger Corp. registration statement on SEC EDGAR (filing date 2026-05-26) states a $65 M PIPE investment, a $75 M public offering, issuance of up to 6,434,293 shares of common stock and a post-merger authorised capitalisation of 200,000,000 shares. Revenue, net loss and cash on hand are NOT disclosed in the document, which states only a "history of net losses"; a supplier-dependence risk factor is present but no export-control risk factor was found [G]

IMEC-300MM-SC-2024-09.text: Van Damme, Massar, Acharya, Potočnik, De Greve et al. (imec / KU Leuven), "Advanced CMOS manufacturing of superconducting qubits on 300 mm wafers", Nature 634, 74-79 (2024-09-18): Al/AlOx/Al overlap junctions patterned by 193 nm immersion lithography and RIE only (no e-beam, no shadow evaporation); 393/400 qubits functional; median T1 75 us, max 113 us, best single qubit 161 us, best T2e 245 us; junction-resistance spread ~8% RSD across the wafer and ~4% within a die over 7,872 test structures; qubit-frequency spread 5-7% RSD [D]

ANDERON-LOI-2026-05.text: IBM newsroom (2026-05-21): Anderon is a standalone "pure-play quantum foundry" in Albany, New York, with IBM as primary investor ($1 B cash plus IP and assets) alongside a proposed $1 B CHIPS award; 300 mm superconducting-qubit and supporting-electronics wafers, intended to serve multiple quantum vendors worldwide; explicitly a letter of intent "subject to negotiation and execution of definitive documents"; no definitive agreement confirmed as of 2026-09-04, though IBM's 2026-08-26 HRL release already calls Anderon "its quantum wafer foundry" [C][G]

OQC-WAFERPKG-AUTHORS-2026-02.text: The >500-qubit wafer-scale package preprint (arXiv:2602.12773) is Kennedy, Ahmad, Armstrong ... Shelly, Oxford Quantum Circuits (Reading, UK), "Design and operation of wafer-scale packages containing >500 superconducting qubits": monolithic 3-inch sapphire die, 56 triangular 9-to-1 readout multiplexing cells, out-of-plane coaxial wiring with no wire bonds and no per-qubit control lines in the measured configuration; median T1 ~97 us and T2e ~129 us (>100 qubits), readout 97.5% median and 36 mK effective temperature (54 qubits), 105/108 qubits operational on the characterised subset [P]

IQM-CZ-9993-2025-08.text: Marxer, Vepsalainen et al. (IQM Quantum Computers, Espoo FI / Munich DE, 68 authors), "Above 99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device", arXiv:2508.16437 (2025-08-22): two transmons joined by a flux-tunable floating transmon coupler; single-qubit fidelity 99.98%, CZ 99.93% averaged over 40 hours, simultaneous readout fidelity above 99.94% using a 240 ns readout pulse with shelving to the second excited state, measurement QNDness 99.3%, TWPA in the readout chain; gate durations not stated in the retrieved text [D]

OXFORD-COAXMON-CZ-2025-03.text: Leek Lab (University of Oxford, presenter S. D. Fasciati), reported by OQC 2025-03-21: controlled-Z at 99.8% fidelity in 25 ns between a standard transmon and an inductively shunted transmon of opposite anharmonicity in the coaxmon architecture, with FIXED coupling and NO tunable coupler - an approximately sqrt(2) speed-up that suppresses ZZ idling error without a coupler flux line; related preprint arXiv:2410.10416. Correction: this result is widely cited as a tunable-coupler record and is not one [C]

HARVARD-CONT-3000-2025-09.text: Harvard (Lukin group), "Continuous operation of a coherent 3,000-qubit system", Nature 646 (online 2025-09-15): 3,217 atoms at 99.3% filling in a 3,240-site array, continuous operation sustained beyond 2 hours (over 50 million atoms cycled by 2.3 h), 300,000 atoms loaded into tweezers per second and 30,000 initialised qubits/s (15,000/s with rearrangement), atoms transported 0.5 m by dual optical-lattice conveyor belts rather than by AODs, T2 = 1.09(3) s with dynamical decoupling and T1 = 3.43(3) s under storage shielding [D]

AOD-3D-LENS-2025-10.text: Guo, van Herk, Vredenbregt, Kokkelmans, "Acousto-optic lens for 3D shuttling of atoms in a neutral atom quantum computer", arXiv:2510.09398 (2025-10-10): double-pass AOD for dynamic focal tuning combined with crossed AODs for transverse steering, giving arbitrary 3D focal trajectories; an optical design and characterisation study with NO trapped atoms - axial range, shuttling speed and atom survival are not demonstrated [S]

AOD-VENDORS-2026.text: Only two acousto-optic deflector suppliers are named across the sourced neutral-atom literature: AA Opto-Electronic (France; DTSX-400 crossed AODs in the Harvard 448-atom system, alongside Hamamatsu SLM/camera, Spectrum Instrumentation AWGs and Rohde & Schwarz microwave sources) and Gooch & Housego (UK; deflectors in the 3,000- and 6,100-qubit papers). Neither is publicly listed or separately funded per this session's checks; no capacity or scale-up figures found [D][P]

PHOTONIC-TCENTRE-DQC-2024-06.text: RESOLVES the ic_spinphoton T-centre vs NV teleported-CNOT conflict: BOTH results exist and differ in kind. Photonic Inc., "Distributed Quantum Computing in Silicon", arXiv:2406.01704 (2024-06-03, no journal publication located as of 2026-09-04): two silicon T-centre modules in SEPARATE CRYOSTATS joined by ~40 m of fibre, native telecom O-band emission near 1326 nm (no frequency conversion); remote Bell-state fidelity F = 0.60(8) at a 40 ns time bin, entanglement generation ~7.5 mHz; a teleported-CNOT (tCNOT) sequence WAS run but all feed-forward was forgone and the result post-selected on photon-detection outcome 00, reported as a truth table over a selected basis with NO gate fidelity stated. By contrast QuTech/Delft's 2026-05-26 NV inter-cryostat teleported CNOT is unconditional (real-time feed-forward, no post-selection) at 63(4)%/64(4)% [P]

HARVARD-SIV-35KM-DETAIL-2024.text: Knaut, Suleymanzade, Wei, Assumpcao, Stas, Huan, Machielse, Bhaskar, Park, Loncar, Lukin (Harvard), "Entanglement of nanophotonic quantum memory nodes in a telecom network", Nature 629 (2024-05-15): SiV emission 737.2 nm converted bidirectionally to 1350 nm; electron-electron entanglement 0.86(3) for
HARVARD-SIV-35KM-DETAIL-2024.date: Phi+> at ~20 m at up to 1 Hz; nuclear-nuclear 0.77(5) with error detection; 0.69(7) through a 35 km deployed Boston urban loop carrying 17 dB loss (also 40 km of spools); nuclear memory over 2 s, entanglement preserved up to 1 s under dynamical decoupling; ~23% of data rejected on reflectance-contrast thresholds [D]

PHOTONIC-PROFILE-2026.text: Photonic Inc. (Vancouver CA; founder Stephanie Simmons, CEO Paul Terry): Microsoft strategic collaboration and investment formed 2023-11; qubits operated at ~1.5-4 K rather than millikelvin; stated milestones May 2024 inter-module distributed entanglement, Feb 2025 qLDPC codes claimed to cut physical-qubit overhead up to 20x, Sep 2025 electrically triggered silicon single-photon source at ~92% spin-initialisation fidelity, Nov 2025 DARPA QBI Stage B; public roadmap is fault-tolerant distributed computing "within five years" of 2023 (~2028) and a long-run link target of ~200 kHz entanglement at 99.8% fidelity — seven orders of magnitude in rate above its own published 7.5 mHz [P][R]

RO-SC-FLEET-GAP-2026.text: Superconducting dispersive-readout error spans three regimes as of 2026-09-04: 6x10^-4 assignment error on a characterised pair (IQM, 99.94% simultaneous readout with a 240 ns pulse and shelving, QNDness 99.3%, arXiv:2508.16437); 5x10^-3 averaged over 105 qubits (Google Willow, readout 99.5%, 1.1 us QEC cycle, Nature 2024-12); ~1x10^-2 across IBM's deployed fleet (ibm.com/quantum/hardware). QNDness, not assignment fidelity, is what syndrome extraction consumes, and no vendor publishes a fleet-average QNDness or a decomposition of the ~1% fleet error [D][C]

TWPA-RPM-2015.text: Josephson travelling-wave parametric amplifier with resonator (minimal) phase matching, arXiv:1503.04364 (2015-03): 12 dB gain across a 4 GHz span with noise approaching the quantum limit - the result that removed the HEMT noise penalty from dispersive readout chains; authors, institution and journal reference not confirmed by the fetch used [D]

IONQ-LIGHTSYNQ-2025-06.text: IonQ completed its acquisition of Lightsynq Technologies on 2025-06-03 (terms undisclosed): photonic interconnect plus quantum-memory/repeater technology for linking quantum processors, founded by Harvard quantum-networking and former AWS researchers Mihir Bhaskar (CEO), Bart Machielse (CTO) and David Levonian (CPO); IonQ states the deal brought "over 20 patents and patent applications"; no interconnect rate, fidelity or scaling target disclosed [C]

IONQ-PHOTONIC-LINK-2026-04.text: IonQ press release 2026-04-14 (AFRL partner, case AFRL-2026-1742) states it "validated the generation, transmission, and detection of photons used to enable quantum entanglement between two commercial IonQ computers at a distance for the first time". NO entanglement rate, Bell-pair fidelity, distance, qubit count or wavelength is disclosed, and the wording stops short of reporting a measured Bell state; no independent replication [C]

ION-PHOTON-2007-ATTRIB.text: The first remote ion-ion entanglement heralded by interfering emitted photons (2007) is from Monroe's group at the University of Michigan (later Maryland/Duke), not the Wineland/NIST line - the same lineage that holds the 250 s-1 rate record (arXiv:2404.16167). Correction to the ic_ionphoton draft, which attributed 2007 to "Wineland group lineage"; the 2007 paper itself was not fetched, so no URL is carried here [D]

EXCHANGE-ONLY-ORIGIN-2000.text: The theoretical basis for baseband-only (microwave-free) universal control is DiVincenzo, Bacon, Kempe, Burkard, Whaley, "Universal quantum computation with the exchange interaction", Nature 408, 339 (2000), arXiv:quant-ph/0005116: the Heisenberg exchange interaction ALONE exactly implements any quantum circuit, eliminating one-qubit operations driven by local Zeeman fields, at a stated cost of a factor of ~3 in additional qubits and ~10 in additional two-qubit operations. This dates the ct_base lineage to 2000 (proposal), not "~2012"; the technology-graph record's since=2012 refers to demonstration and was not re-verified [S]

QUTECH-BASEBAND-BOUND-2025.text: CORRECTION on how the QuTech baseband hopping-gate number should be quoted: the 99.50(6)% figure in Unseld, Undseth, Raymenants et al. (Nature Communications, 2025-07-01) is a LOWER BOUND on hopping-gate fidelity, and the Hahn-echo coherence is "up to ~49 us", not a typical value; both are frequently restated as point estimates [D]

HRL-LAMBDA-CAVEAT-2026.text: Reading caveat for HRL's spin-qubit QEC result: the Lambda(5/3) = 4.7 and 5.0e-3 logical error over 200 rounds are for a distance-5 REPETITION code, which detects bit-flips only, so they are not evidence of below-threshold operation of a full code; the accompanying [[4,2,2]] logical fidelity of 0.95 is post-selected. The main report's cross-cutting table already flags the spin entry as "repetition d=5 Lambda=4.7 (bit-flip only)" [D]

PRINCETON-ERASURE-RESOLVED-2026-09.text: CONFLICT RESOLVED: the 1.9(4)x and 3.6x figures both appear in arXiv:2506.13724v2 (Princeton [[4,2,2]] metastable 171-Yb) and describe different quantities — the logical decay rate during hold is "3.6(1) times slower when including the erasure information" for the POST-SELECTED logical qubit, while under UNCONDITIONAL decoding "the decay rate with increasing hold time is reduced by a factor of 1.9(4)"; same paper also gives AR CZ error 0.016(1) with 38(6)% detected as erasures, time-optimal CZ error 0.011(1), teleportation 0.771(9) rising to 0.87(2) post-selected on no erasure. Only 1.9(4)x is architecturally meaningful; supersedes the "unreconciled" status in PRINCETON-ERASURE-2026-06 and PRINCETON-ERASURE-V2-2026-06

SCHAEFER-FASTGATE-2018.text: ATTRIBUTION FIX: the "fastest laser two-qubit gate" record (99.8% fidelity at 1.6 us) is Schaefer, Ballance, Thirumalai, Stephenson, Ballance, Steane, Lucas (Oxford), "Fast quantum logic gates with trapped-ion qubits", Nature 555 / arXiv:1709.06952 (2018) - frequently mis-cited as "Ballance et al." The abstract adds: 43Ca+ hyperfine qubits, laser pulses shaped on 10 ns timescales, entanglement still generated at a gate time of 480 ns (less than one motional oscillation period, no fidelity quoted for that point), gate error "more than ten times lower" than conventional techniques whose speed limit is of order 10 kHz [D]

IONQ-30Q-BENCH-2023.text: The IonQ Molmer-Sorensen gate-duration figures (550-883 us, median 672 us, 1Q 110 us) come from Chen, Nielsen, Ebert, Inlek, Wright, Chaplin, Maksymov, Paez, Poudel, Maunz, Gamble (IonQ), "Benchmarking a trapped-ion quantum computer with 30 qubits", arXiv:2308.05071 (2023-08-09, rev. 2024-11-02). The abstract specifies a SINGLE-CHAIN 30-qubit configuration with all-to-all operations benchmarked across all 435 gate pairs - so "30+-ion chains" should read "one 30-ion chain"; the duration range itself is in the full text, not the abstract [D]

AQT-LYNX-QV-CONTEXT-2026.text: READING CAVEAT for the AQT LYNX "quantum volume record": QV 32,768 = 2^15, against QV 2^25 published for Quantinuum's 56-qubit H2 - roughly three orders of magnitude lower, so the claim is a record within the rack-mounted/commercially-shipped class, not a field record. AQT discloses neither gate time nor fidelity behind the number [C]

DELFT-CIRCUITS-FUNDING-2025-12.text: Delft Circuits (Cri/oFlex cryogenic RF cabling) announced a EUR 8 M Series A extension on 2025-12-03, bringing cumulative funding to EUR 15 M; existing shareholders DeepTech XL, High Tech Gruenderfonds and QuVest plus new investors Paeonia Group and Waves Capital Partners; Martin Danoesastro named CEO the same day; a Series B was said to be in preparation for 2026 [P]

QBLOX-SERIESA-2024-06.text: Qblox (modular room-temperature qubit control stacks) closed a USD 26 M Series A announced 2024-06-20, co-led by Quantonation and the Invest-NL Deep Tech fund with QDNL Participations and the European Innovation Council; company claims "over one hundred customers" and states it grew on revenue rather than investment; cumulative funding not disclosed [C]

KRINNER-CRYO-WIRING-2019.text: Krinner, Storz, Kurpiers, Magnard, Heinsoo, Keller, Luetolf, Eichler, Wallraff (ETH Zurich), "Engineering cryogenic setups for 100-qubit scale superconducting circuit systems", EPJ Quantum Technology 6, 2 (2019; arXiv:1806.07862): measured passive loads of stainless-steel and NbTi coax plus active signal dissipation in a Bluefors XLD400 (~40-50 W at 50 K, ~1 W at 4 K); the described setup supports 50 qubits at 14 mK with 25 drive and 25 flux lines, and "at least 150 qubits could be operated" disregarding space constraints — the canonical per-fridge line-count/thermal bound [D]

EXCHANGE-BEST-GATE-2026.text: CORRECTION on "best demonstrated exchange gate": the leading number is HRL's exchange-only CNOT at 9x10^-4 best reproducible (99.91%), 3x10^-3 mean over 18 qubits built from 54 dots (arXiv:2604.16216, Nature 2026-07-29) - NOT SQC's 99.90% donor nuclear CZ, which is a nuclear-spin gate mediated by hyperfine coupling to a shared electron rather than a voltage-pulsed exchange gate between electron spins. Foundry electron-exchange pairs (Diraq/imec 300 mm) sit at 99.04-99.56% [D]

SQC-11Q-MECHANISM-2025.text: Mechanism and value conflict for the SQC 11-qubit donor result (arXiv:2506.03567; Nature 648, 569-575, 2025-12-17): the abstract describes TWO multi-nuclear-spin registers, qubits within a register coupled by hyperfine interaction to a single shared electron, the two registers linked by electron exchange - so exchange enters only as the inter-register link. Fidelity framings conflict three ways: arXiv abstract "all fidelities ranging from 99.5% to 99.99%" and Bell "beyond 99%"; fact record row SQC-11Q-2025-12 (published version) "99.10-99.99%, Bell up to 99.5%"; main report a single "99.90% donor nuclear-spin CZ". The 99.90% could not be isolated in the abstract [D]

DWAVE-FLUXDAC-LINECOUNT-CONFLICT.text: D-Wave states two different bias-wire counts for the same annealer control scheme seventeen days apart: the press release of 2026-01-06 says "the control technology uses multiplexed digital-to-analog converters to control tens of thousands of qubits and couplers with just 200 bias wires", while whitepaper 14-1090A-A of 2026-01-23 quotes ~300 bias lines for several-thousand qubits plus tens-of-thousands of couplers. Unreconciled; the whitepaper figure is the one tied to a described array. The same release states key components of the fluxonium multichip package were fabricated at NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory

SHENZHEN-UNIFIEDFLUX-2026-05.text: Pan, Wang, Zhou, Deng, Wang et al. (S Lab, Quantum Science Center of Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, Shenzhen), "Unified Flux Control Architecture for Fluxonium Qubits", arXiv:2605.25948 (2026-05-26): experimentally realises XY and Z operations for a fluxonium through a single flux-control channel driven by one AWG channel; 8 devices (A-H), single-qubit gate fidelity 99.99% on device A and >=99.97% on B-E, T1 110 us / T2-Ramsey 128 us / T2-echo 133 us, 20 ns gates, reset ~98%, qubit frequencies 164-378 MHz, 92 MHz low-pass, >50 dB line attenuation; room-temperature AWGs, NO on-chip DACs, no crosstalk figures given [D]

DUKE-SNSPD-IONREAD-2019.text: Crain, Cahall, Vrijsen, Wollman, Shaw, Verma, Nam, Kim (Duke University Fitzpatrick Institute for Photonics, JPL/Caltech, NIST), "High-speed low-crosstalk detection of a 171Yb+ qubit using superconducting nanowire single photon detectors", Communications Physics 2, 97 (2019-08-21): 99.931(6)% detection fidelity in 11 microseconds average, MoSi SNSPD optimised for 369.5 nm UV, crosstalk error ~2x10^-5 at 370 um ion separation; the high efficiency and low dark count let the experiment stop on a single detection event — the origin of the "11 us at 99.93%" ion-readout record [D]

MITLL-TRAPAPD-2022.text: Reens, Collins, Ciampi, Kharas, Aull, Donlon, Bruzewicz, Felton, Stuart, Niffenegger, Rich, Braje, Ryu, Chiaverini, McConnell (MIT Lincoln Laboratory), "High-fidelity ion state detection using trap-integrated avalanche photodiodes", Phys. Rev. Lett. 129, 100502 (2022-09-02): 99.92(1)% average detection fidelity in 450 microseconds using room-temperature single-photon avalanche diodes fabricated into the ion trap itself, Sr+ ions; the authors note a separate detector per trapping site would enable parallel readout — the integration path for zone counts beyond free-space optics [D]

KYOTO-FASTIMG-CORRECTION.text: CORRECTION: the Kyoto University / Yaqumo 17.6 us imaging result (arXiv:2605.24175, KYOTO-FASTIMG-2026-08) measures NEUTRAL 174-Yb atoms on an EMCCD, not trapped ions; it must not be cited as a trapped-ion fluorescence-readout record. Its transferable content is methodological — it reports discrimination (99.89%) and survival (98.80%) separately, which trapped-ion SPAM figures generally do not [P]

HARVARD-CONTINUOUS-RELOAD-2025.text: RESOLVES the 30,000 vs 300,000 atoms/s conflict. Chiu, Ji, Bluvstein et al. (Harvard/MIT/QuEra), "Continuous operation of a coherent 3,000-qubit system", Nature (s41586-025-09596-6): verbatim abstract - "Using a reloading rate of 300,000 atoms in tweezers per second, we create over 30,000 initialized qubits per second, which we leverage to assemble and maintain an array of over 3,000 atoms for more than 2 hours." Both figures are correct and differently scoped: 300,000/s = raw extraction into optical tweezers from the reservoir, 30,000/s = initialized qubits after preparation. Transport is by a series of TWO optical-lattice conveyor belts carrying reservoirs into the science region, not by AODs; extraction does not disturb the coherence of qubits stored nearby [D]

TOPTICA-FACTS-2026.text: TOPTICA Photonics (Munich) company page states EUR 140 M annual revenue, 600 employees, over 26 years of operation, group companies TOPTICA EAGLEYARD (laser diodes, in-group since 2013) and TOPTICA PROJECTS, offices in Rochester NY and Bordeaux plus TOPTICA Japan and TOPTICA China; describes quantum technology as "the TOPTICA DNA since the founding of the company" and names quantum computing, simulation, sensing, atomic clocks and communication as served markets. This corroborates the EUR 140 M / 600-staff figures previously carried only from postquantum.com; the separate "dominant supplier to trapped-ion systems" framing remains single-sourced to that trade analysis [C]

ATOM-OPTICS-UNIT-COST-2026.text: Two publicly quotable turnkey prices bracket the optical/mechanical assembly tier and differ by about two orders per qubit: QuNorth's order of the 1,225-physical / 50-logical "Magne" neutral-atom system from Atom Computing and Microsoft at EUR 80 M (~EUR 65 k per physical atom), against AQT's 20-qubit trapped-ion system delivered to the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre for ~EUR 9.8 M (~EUR 0.5 M per ion). Tweezer optics amortise across thousands of sites; ion optics scale closer to per-ion [P][C]
ATOM-OPTICS-UNIT-COST-2026.value: EUR 65 k vs EUR 0.5 M per qubit

SANDIA-PHOTONICS-NOMETRIC-2026-08.text: Sandia National Laboratories Lab News (2026-08-27) on the renewed four-year Quantinuum CRADA gives NO component-level metric for its MESA integrated photonics: it quotes only Helios system fidelities (99.9975% 1Q, 99.921% 2Q) and the qualitative claim that integrated photonics "promise to reduce the risks of quantum technology by lowering energy costs and improving scalability". No waveguide loss, crosstalk, wavelength or zone count is disclosed by Sandia [G]

MPQ-CAVITY-REGISTER-2024.text: Hartung, Seubert, Welte, Distante, Rempe (Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics), "A quantum-network register assembled with optical tweezers in an optical cavity", Science 385, 179-183 (2024); arXiv:2407.09109 submitted 2024-07-12: two-dimensional atom array assembled with optical tweezers and lattices inside an optical cavity, single-atom addressing, multiplexed atom-photon entanglement with generation-to-detection efficiency approaching 90%. NOTE: the "cavity-carved Bell-state fidelity 91%" figure circulating in derived material is NOT in the abstract and was not confirmed [D]

UIUC-TELECOM-YB-NET-2025.text: Li, Hu, Jia, Huie, Sun, Aakash, Dong, Hiri-O-Tuppa, Covey (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign), "Parallelized telecom quantum networking with an ytterbium-171 atom array", Nature Physics 21 (published online 2025-09-12): time-bin atom-photon entanglement emitted directly at 1389 nm (telecom band, no lossy frequency conversion), atom array imaged onto an optical fibre array so the remote-entanglement rate scales proportionally with channel count; no absolute rate given in the abstract [D]

NUQ-SERIESA-DATE-CORRECTION.text: CORRECTION: Nu Quantum's $60 M Series A closed on 2025-12-10 led by National Grid Partners (see NUQ-SERIESA-2025-12), not on 2026-06-17 with an undisclosed lead. The 2026-06-17 Atom Computing MoU coverage (ATOM-NUQUANTUM-2026-06) merely restated the earlier round; do not log it as a second financing event [C]

C2N-GRAPHSTATE-2025-05.text: Coste, Senellart et al. (C2N, Université Paris-Saclay), "Deterministic and reconfigurable graph state generation with a single solid-state quantum emitter," Nature Communications, 2025-05-09: InGaAs quantum dot in a GaAs micropillar cavity produces reconfigurable 4-photon entangled graph states at ~0.5 Hz useful 4-photon rate, Bell fidelity up to 0.80 +/- 0.04, concurrence up to 0.69 +/- 0.09, 4-partite linear cluster fidelity 0.66 +/- 0.05; a 10-photon caterpillar state is projected, not measured. Second-best emitter-based graph-state result after the 2024 MPQ 8-photon fusion record [D]

YALE-BS-SQUID-2023-03.text: The ~100 ns cavity-cavity beam-splitter swap "exceeding 99.98%" (arXiv:2303.00959, 2023-03) is mediated by a differentially driven DC-SQUID coupler, not a SNAIL; the arXiv abstract page returns body text only, so author list, affiliation and journal reference remain unconfirmed [D]

YALE-BS-LINEAGE-2018.text: Ancilla/coupler-mediated bosonic gates date to Yale's "Programmable interference between two microwave quantum memories" (arXiv:1802.08510, 2018-02-23; PRX 8, 021073): an RF-driven, time-dependent bilinear coupling acting as a tunable 50:50 beam-splitter between two superconducting cavity modes, with Hong-Ou-Mandel interference and cascaded Mach-Zehnder interferometers; no fidelity or timing numbers in the abstract — this anchors the "since 2018" date for the mechanism [D]

DWAVE-DR-CZ-MARKETING-2026-08.text: D-Wave markets the Nature dual-rail cavity CZ as "approximately 99.9%" two-qubit fidelity at ~500 ns [C], which reconciles with neither the ~99.5% raw (0.5% erasure per gate) nor the 99.971% post-selected value (0.029(6)% Pauli) reported in the paper; treat 99.9% as a marketing figure, not a measured gate fidelity

BSM-LINOPT-CEILING.text: Linear-optical Bell-state measurement ceiling: with passive linear optics and vacuum ancillae only, unambiguous discrimination of the four Bell states succeeds at 50% at best; adding unentangled single-photon ancillae raises it to at least 75% (Ewert & van Loock, "3/4-efficient Bell measurement with passive linear optics and unentangled ancillae", Phys. Rev. Lett. 113, 140403, arXiv:1403.4841, 2014-03-19); the paper notes the construction extends toward 100% with more ancillae. This is the information-theoretic basis for the 50%/75% fusion success figures used across the photonic briefs [S]

TFLN-SQUEEZING-2025-08.text: Shi, Baiju, Chen, Mohanraj, Wang, Dhyani, Shajilal, Zhao, Yang, Li, Wu, Hao, Leong, Lam, Zhu, "Squeezed light generation in periodically poled thin-film lithium niobate waveguides," arXiv:2508.08599 (2025-08-12, v2 2025-10-29), published in Nanophotonics: 1.4 dB squeezing directly measured by homodyne detection with 4 dB total detection loss, over 10 dB inferred (loss-corrected) at 62 mW pump, on periodically poled TFLN nanophotonic waveguides. This is RAW quadrature squeezing and is NOT the same quantity as Xanadu's 0.62 dB on-chip GKP effective squeezing; the two must not be compared directly [D]

MEMS-SWITCH-2026-08.text: Roy, Klawson, Luo, Zhi, Tang, Wu, "Zero-change foundry compatible silicon photonics MEMS optical switch", arXiv:2608.03146 (2026-08-04): C-band MEMS switch made by BEOL post-processing of a standard foundry die, insertion loss < 1.5 dB, extinction ratio > 30 dB, ~20 nW static power at maximum actuation voltage; switching time and crosstalk not stated in the retrievable abstract, institutional affiliations not returned by the arXiv abstract page [P]

PHOTONIC-MESH-LINEAGE-2015.text: Programmable photonic switching meshes date to Carolan et al., "Universal Linear Optics" (arXiv:1505.01182, 2015): a single reprogrammable six-mode circuit of 15 cascaded Mach-Zehnder interferometers with 30 thermo-optic phase shifters, up to six input photons and 12 single-photon detectors, average fidelity 0.999 +/- 0.001 over 100 random unitaries, reconfigurable "in seconds" - thermo-optic and second-scale, the opposite end of the speed/power axis from fusion-based fault tolerance; this anchors the "since 2015" date for the switching layer [D]

SWITCH-LOSS-REFERENCE-PLANES-2026.text: Photonic switch-loss figures in circulation are NOT comparable and must not be summed or ranked: Xanadu Aurora 0.19 dB is per MZI including interconnect (Nature, 2025-01); PsiQuantum Omega 100 mdB is the barium-titanate switch element alone and is the best published in-line figure (Nature, 2025-02), roughly 14x the ~7 mdB fault-tolerance allowance; Xanadu's 0.085 dB/facet (2026-06-10) is fibre-to-chip coupling marketed as an industry benchmark although PsiQuantum published 52(12) mdB for the same interface a year earlier; the 1.48 dB/cell non-volatile BTO array (2026-06-04) is a static-power result. The cx_switch technology-graph record's "recent 30 mdB" figure could not be traced to any publication

FBQC-THRESHOLD-CONFLICT-2026.text: Conflicting 6-ring loss thresholds for fusion-based fault tolerance as of 2026-09-04: arXiv:2506.11975 (2025-06, quoted in the main report and the fusion-based fault-tolerance brief) gives 2.7% loss per photon for a BOOSTED 6-ring resource state and 17.4% for a {7,4}-encoded state (described elsewhere as ~168 photons), while Loebl et al., arXiv:2606.28490 (2026-06-26) give 0.38-0.82% (static bias) and 0.78% (random bias) for an UNENCODED 6-ring, plus 7.0-7.3% for hybrid emitter-mediated fusion. Boosting, bias model and decoder assumptions differ, so the figures are not directly comparable; no source reconciles them [S]

TWEEZER-LINEAGE-2016.text: Optical-tweezer array control dates to Endres et al., "Cold Matter Assembled Atom-by-Atom" (arXiv:1607.03044, submitted 2016-07-11): real-time control of 100 optical tweezers producing defect-free arrays of over 50 atoms in under 400 ms by a measurement-and-feedback procedure that also replaces lost atoms from a reservoir; institutional affiliation is not stated on the retrievable arXiv abstract page. This anchors the "since 2016" date for laser/AOD/SLM atom control, and its measure-decide-move-verify loop is still the neutral-atom clock in 2026 [D]

SLM-REFRESH-CLAIM-UNSOURCED.text: CAUTION: the main report's "SLM/AOD 10 MHz refresh insufficient above ~10^4 qubits" cannot be attributed to any device or measurement in the sourced literature. Liquid-crystal-on-silicon modulators frame at tens of hertz and are effectively static within a shot; acousto-optic deflector reconfiguration is bounded below by the acoustic transit time across the beam, and the deflector's resolvable-spot count is RF bandwidth times that same transit — so spot count and re-pointing speed trade against each other in one device. Treat 10 MHz as an order-of-magnitude proxy, not a device parameter

TWEEZER-POWER-SCALING-2026.text: Trap-power scaling law for tweezer arrays, derived from TSINGHUA-METASURFACE-2026-06: 33 W incident / 12.2 W effective across 18,225 sites is ~0.67 mW of effective trapping power per site, and the relation is linear in site count, so 10^6 sites implies of order 1 kW of effective trapping light before any imaging, cooling or Rydberg beam. Compare the Fraunhofer ILT/Stuttgart delivered system at 20 W for 2,000 tweezers (~10 mW/site at 3.5 um pitch) - per-site power is geometry-dependent and the two must not be averaged [D]

OCELOT-BIAS-CORRECTION-2025.text: CORRECTION to figures in circulation: in the AWS/Caltech Ocelot paper (Putterman et al., Nature 638, 927-934, 2025-02-26) the CX gate at

Repetition-code logical error is 1.75(2)% at distance 3 (

MILUL-CAVITY-2023.text: CORRECTION of attribution: the 34 ms cavity result is Milul, Guttel, Goldblatt, Hazanov, Joshi, Chausovsky, Kahn, Ciftyurek, Lafont, Rosenblum, WEIZMANN INSTITUTE (not Yale-lineage), PRX Quantum 4, 030336 (2023-09-14): single-photon lifetime T1 = 25.6 ms, coherence T2 = 34 ms, 1024-photon cat state, from a cavity geometry that "couples minimally to the control qubit"; no niobium coating is stated in the abstract or journal summary. Best published superconducting cavity memory as of 2026-09-04; single-group, unreplicated

ALICEBOB-ROADMAP-2026-09.text: Alice & Bob public roadmap as retrieved 2026-09-04: Boson 4 (1 cat, complete 2024) -> Helium (12-18 cats, 1 logical, target logical error 10^-2, "we are here") -> Lithium (48 cats, 4 logical, 10^-3) -> Beryllium (250 cats, 5 logical, 10^-4) -> Graphene (2,000 cats, 100 logical, 10^-6, 2030); the page attaches a 13-minute bit-flip requirement to the Graphene chip and states a September 2025 PEAK bit-flip of 252 minutes (against the 44-minute mean reported for the same 12-cat run) [C]

FLUXONIUM-CNOT-2024-07.text: Lin, Cho, Chen, Vavilov, Wang, Manucharyan (Maryland, Wisconsin, UMass Amherst, EPFL), "24 days-stable CNOT-gate on fluxonium qubits with over 99.9% fidelity", PRX Quantum 6, 010349 (2025); arXiv:2407.15783 (2024-07-22): CNOT 99.94% (infidelity 6x10^-4) in 60 ns, above 99.9% for 24 days with no recalibration; T1 260/160 us, T2* 100/110 us, T2-echo 200/150 us; dominant error = off-resonant control-qubit flips, coherent error below 2x10^-4 — supersedes the report's 99.92% MIT fluxonium record [D]

MIT-FLUXONIUM-CZ-2023.text: Ding, Hays, Sung, ... Serniak, Oliver (MIT / MIT Lincoln Laboratory), Phys. Rev. X 13, 031035 (2023-09-25): fluxonium CZ with transmon coupler, peak CZ fidelities 99.85-99.9%, reinforcement-learning-optimised MEAN 99.922 +/- 0.009% — the widely quoted "99.92% fluxonium record" is an RL-optimised mean, and the abstract states no gate duration (the "50 ns" carried in the technology-graph record is unconfirmed) [D]

MIT-FLUXONIUM-1Q-2025.text: MIT EQuS with MIT Lincoln Laboratory, "Suppressing Counter-Rotating Errors for Fast Single-Qubit Gates with Fluxonium" (PRX Quantum; MIT News 2025-01-14): single-qubit gate fidelity 99.998% on fluxonium [D]

QUIX-FFCU-2026-06.text: QuiX Quantum installed a rack-mounted Feed-Forward Control Unit (announced 2026-06-02): approximately 150 ns from single-photon-detector input signal to settled output drive voltage on integrated Mach-Zehnder interferometers, two FPGA modules on a low-latency bus, 32 inputs and 32 outputs; QuiX frames it as the prerequisite for universality in its 2026 universal photonic machine and notes light travels ~30 m in telecom fibre in 150 ns [C]

FPGA-FEEDFORWARD-196NS-2026-06.text: Duggan, Filgis, Bregnsbo, Saalmueller, Neergaard-Nielsen, Wintermantel, Andersen, "FPGA Based Feedforward System for Photonic Quantum Computing Applications", arXiv:2606.03500 (2026-06-02, v2 2026-06-25): 196 ns total system latency for real-time adaptive measurement and displacement in continuous-variable measurement-based protocols; homodyne detector clearance 15 dB at 1 GHz, local-oscillator power 4 mW, quantum efficiency >95%; institutional affiliations not stated on the retrievable abstract page [P]

FEEDFORWARD-DELAY-LOSS-2026.text: Derived architectural constraint for photonic feed-forward: 100 ns of optical hold in single-mode SiN is ~15 m of waveguide at group index ~2, which at the measured 1.8(2) dB/m Omega loss is ~27 dB - impossible against a ~0.5 dB per-photon budget; the same 100 ns in standard fibre is ~20 m at 0.2 dB/km (~4 mdB) plus two fibre-to-chip transitions at 52(12) mdB each. Feed-forward delay must therefore be held off-chip in fibre, making the loss cost of feed-forward a packaging number rather than a waveguide number [S]

METRO-ENT-155KM-2024-09.text: "Entanglement distribution over 155 km metropolitan fiber using a CMOS-compatible silicon chip", arXiv:2409.17558 (2024-09): 8 mm silicon nanophotonic waveguide pair source distributing entanglement over deployed Singapore metropolitan fibre linking NUS, SUTD and NTU; 0.7 coincidences/s through 66 dB total channel loss (56 dB fibre + 10 dB dispersion compensation) at 155 km with 87.6(5)% measured fidelity, versus 132 coincidences/s and 93.3(3)% at 93 km. The only published loss-versus-rate exchange curve usable as a reference for photonic inter-module links; authors and affiliations not returned by the abstract fetch [P]

FIBRE-MODULE-COST-2026.text: Derived cost of a photonic module boundary: crossing between two photonic chips costs two fibre-to-chip transitions at 52(12) mdB each (~104 mdB, roughly one fifth of a ~0.5 dB per-photon fault-tolerance budget), while the 42 m span itself costs only ~8 mdB at 0.2 dB/km - so photonic modularity is priced per interface, not per metre. In time the reverse holds: 42 m is ~206 ns one way at group index 1.47, longer than the best 2026 feed-forward loop (~150 ns), so module separation consumes the decision budget before the loss budget [S]

USTC-LEAKAGE-2025-12.text: He, Lin, Wang, Li et al. (Hefei National Laboratory / USTC, Pan group), "Experimental Quantum Error Correction below the Surface Code Threshold via All-Microwave Leakage Suppression", Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 260601 (2025-12-22): distance-7 surface code, Lambda = 1.40(6), leakage suppressed 72x, residual leakage population 6.4(5)x10^-4 after 40 cycles. NOTE: the PRL itself does not name the processor - the "Zuchongzhi 3.2" label used in the report is external to the paper [D]

CV-TIMEDOMAIN-LINEAGE-2013.text: ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION: large-scale time-domain multiplexing of continuous-variable cluster states is not a Xanadu first. Yokoyama, Ukai, Armstrong, Sornphiphatphong, Kaji, Suzuki, Yoshikawa, Yonezawa, Menicucci, Furusawa (University of Tokyo), "Ultra-large-scale continuous-variable cluster states multiplexed in the time domain", Nature Photonics, published 2013-11-17, entangled more than 10,000 modes. Xanadu's Aurora (2025-01) is the first modular, chip-based, fibre-networked version, not the first time-domain-multiplexed one [D]

XANADU-GKP-SOURCE-2025-06.text: Xanadu, "Integrated photonic source of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill qubits", Nature, published 2025-06-05: first GKP qubit generated on a fully integrated silicon-nitride photonic chip fabricated on 300 mm wafers and operating at ROOM TEMPERATURE; 0.62 dB effective squeezing per the fact-checked main report, against the ~10 dB the architecture assumes. CTO Zachary Vernon states further optical-loss reduction is what is needed for fault-tolerance-grade GKP states. Note 0.62 dB effective squeezing is not commensurable with raw quadrature squeezing figures such as the 1.4 dB TFLN result [D]

CR-KANDALA-2021-DETAIL.text: ATTRIBUTION FIX for Kandala et al., PRL 127, 130501 (2021-09-22): the 99.77(2)% CNOT is a SINGLE-PULSE gate of 180 ns on an isolated fixed-frequency pair, and the static ZZ is suppressed INTRINSICALLY by two fixed-frequency coupling elements that retune the dressed level spacings (over 6x improvement in wanted-to-unwanted coupling ratio, coherence above 100 us) — not by active cancellation drives, as secondary accounts state [D]

CR-NO-FLEET-NUMBER.text: CAUTION: no fleet-average or device-wide cross-resonance two-qubit fidelity was ever published for IBM's fixed-frequency generations (Falcon-Condor, 2019-2023); the only sourced CR figure is the isolated-pair 99.77(2)%. IBM's published EPLG figures (typical 3.7x10^-3, best 1.9x10^-3, July 2026) are Heron-class tunable-coupler hardware, which replaced CR from 2023-12

RO-S2C-SEB-PRX-2023.text: ATTRIBUTION for the "99.2% in <6 us" spin readout figure: Oakes, Ciriano-Tejel, Wise, Fogarty, Lundberg, Laine, Schaal, Martins, Ibberson, Hutin, Bertrand, Vinet, Stelmashenko, Robinson, Lee, Smith, Morton, Gonzalez-Zalba (Quantum Motion with Cavendish Laboratory/Cambridge, London Centre for Nanotechnology/UCL, CEA-Leti, Hitachi Cambridge, Bristol, UC Berkeley), "Fast High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout of Spins in Silicon Using a Single-Electron Box", Physical Review X 13, 011023, 2023-02-23. Mechanism is a radio-frequency SINGLE-ELECTRON BOX (gate-based dispersive/quantum-capacitance sensing), NOT a galvanic single-electron transistor; the device was made at CEA-Leti [D]

CROSSBAR-16DOT-2024.text: Borsoi, Hendrickx, John, Meyer, Motz, van Riggelen, de Snoo, Scappucci, Veldhorst (QuTech/TU Delft), "Shared control of a 16 semiconductor quantum dot crossbar array", Nature Nanotechnology (online 2023-08-28, issue 2024-01): 16 Ge dots addressed by 23 shared terminals (7 plunger + 16 barrier lines), scaling T = 6*sqrt(g) - 1 for g dots; demonstrated odd (single-hole) occupancy in every site, a statistical method to map multidot charge-stability diagrams to individual dots, and selective interdot-coupling control with tunnel coupling tunable beyond 10 GHz. PROOF OF PRINCIPLE ONLY - no coherent qubit operation on the 16 dots, no two-qubit gate, no crosstalk figure [D]

HRL-ENCODING-ATTRIB-2026.text: ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION repeatedly needed in spin briefs: HRL's 18 qubits from 54 dots, mean 1Q error 2x10^-4 and mean CNOT 3x10^-3 (best reproducible 9x10^-4) are EXCHANGE-ONLY encoded qubits (three dots per qubit), not single-spin (Loss-DiVincenzo) qubits; the ~80%-extrinsic CNOT error attribution likewise belongs to the exchange-only encoding. Drafts have quoted these as Loss-DiVincenzo records. Separately, the "only one of four pairs gates" result belongs to imec/Diraq's individually wired 8-qubit 300 mm device (Nature Communications 17, 5878, 2026-07-09), not to any crossbar device [D]

TIMEBIN-ORIGIN-1999.text: Time-bin (pulsed energy-time) entangled photon pairs were introduced by Brendel, Gisin, Tittel, Zbinden (University of Geneva), "Pulsed energy-time entangled twin-photon source for quantum communication", Phys. Rev. Lett. 82, 2594 (1999), arXiv quant-ph/9809034: a pulsed source of energy-time entangled pairs pumped by a standard laser diode, proposed and demonstrated because "the entanglement is well protected during photon propagation in telecom optical fibers". This anchors the encoding's lineage; the arXiv abstract page returns the abstract text but not the author list, so the attribution rests on the identifier [D]

TIMEBIN-VS-PATH-DELAY-COST.text: Architectural split inside the "time-bin / path" node: a 1 ns time-bin separation needs ~0.15 m of on-chip delay at group index ~2, costing ~0.27 dB at the measured 1.8(2) dB/m single-mode SiN loss - over half a ~0.5 dB per-photon fault-tolerance budget for one bin - versus ~0.04 mdB for the same nanosecond in standard fibre. This is why on-chip machines (PsiQuantum Omega) are PATH-encoded while fibre systems are time-bin encoded; the two halves are one node only in the abstract. Separately, with Omega's median on-chip SNSPD efficiency of 93.4%, roughly 1 heralded event in 15 is an unflagged loss, which bounds the erasure advantage [S]

RT-DECODE-LIVE-GAP-2026.text: Gap as of 2026-09-04: no FPGA decoder has closed the correction loop on LIVE syndromes above distance 3. Riverlane's LCD (<1 us/round to d=17, Nat. Commun. 16, 11048) and Yale's Micro Blossom (0.8 us average at d=13, ASPLOS 2025) are decoder-in-isolation measurements on replayed or simulated syndromes; IBM's Relay-BP FPGA study (arXiv:2510.21600) is simulation-driven; the only live closed loop is the d=3 superconducting demonstration by IQA Shenzhen/SUSTech/Peking/Hefei (arXiv:2605.04892, 550 ns loop). Google's d=7 record used a real-time NEURAL decoder (AlphaQubit2), not matching

DWAVE-SKYWATER-IONQ-EXPOSURE-2026.text: D-Wave's only publicly traceable foundry name (nine "SkyWater" hits in its 10-Ks 2023-2026) became an IonQ subsidiary when the IonQ/SkyWater acquisition closed 2026-07-31, i.e. D-Wave's plausible second-source superconducting foundry now sits inside a direct gate-model competitor [G]

DWAVE-REBUTTAL-2508.text: Nocera, Raymond, Bernoudy, Amin, King (D-Wave/UBC), "Evaluating classical simulations with a quantum processor", arXiv:2508.15759 (2025-08-21): uses the annealing QPU as ground truth for tensor-network methods "whose scaling has not yet been firmly established" and reports observations contrary to previous scaling predictions - D-Wave's formal counter to the Tindall and Mauron/Carleo rebuttals [P]

MSFT-MAJ2-PAPER-2026-06.text: The "Majorana 2" result is Aghaee et al. (Microsoft Quantum, ~200 authors), "20 Second Parity Lifetime in an InAs-Pb Tetron Device", arXiv:2606.03884 (v1 2026-06-02): interferometric single-shot parity measurement of ONE hybrid nanowire of ONE tetron in a multi-tetron array; h/2e-periodic bimodal quantum-capacitance shifts of a coupled quantum dot; characteristic parity switching time ~20 s with some instances minute-scale; a new rf technique resolves wire-end-state energy splitting to ueV precision. The paper reports NO braiding, NO joint/X-basis parity measurement, NO two-qubit operation, NO entanglement and NO qubit T1/T2; it only "discusses potential implications for the fidelity of Pauli measurements". Microsoft's blog restates the ~20 s as a "qubit lifetime" [D]

LEGG-MATTERSARISING-2026-06-24.text: Henry F. Legg (Univ. of St Andrews / Univ. of Basel), "On the robustness of topological gap detection via transport", Nature Matters Arising, published 2026-06-24 (preprint arXiv:2503.08944), against Microsoft Azure Quantum, Nature 638, 651-655 (2025). Claim: the topological gap protocol (TGP) can label the same phase-space regions gapped or gapless depending on data-analysis parameters, and public conductance data absent from the original paper show the regions where the parity readout was performed to be highly disordered and gapless, so the signals may be trivial. Microsoft's multi-author Reply was published the same day (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10568-7) and concedes nothing [D]

MSFT-PARITY-NATURE-2025-02-19.text: Microsoft Azure Quantum, "Interferometric single-shot parity measurement in InAs-Al hybrid devices", Nature 638, 651-655, published 2025-02-19: dispersive gate sensing of quantum capacitance via rf reflectometry off an off-chip resonator, quantum dots tunnel-coupled to a gate-defined superconducting InAs-Al nanowire forming a parity-sensitive interferometer; 1% parity assignment error, SNR 1 in 3.6 us at optimal flux, dwell/parity lifetime longer than 1 ms at ~2 T in-plane field. Nature attached an editor's note that the results do not by themselves establish the presence of Majorana zero modes [D]

ANALOG-CLAIM-STATUS-2026-09.text: As of 2026-09-04 no analog/annealing platform holds an unchallenged beyond-classical claim: D-Wave's Mar-2025 spin-glass quench claim (arXiv:2403.00910) was eroded by Tindall et al. (arXiv:2503.05693) and Mauron & Carleo (arXiv:2503.08247) and countered by D-Wave (arXiv:2508.15759); Google's 69-qubit analog-digital simulator claims beyond-classical only on XEB-style benchmarking; QuEra's Aquila gauge-theory result makes no advantage claim

IONQ-FORTE-435PAIRS-2023-08.text: IonQ Forte benchmarking (arXiv:2308.05071, 2023-08): single chain of 30 ions with all 435 qubit pairs individually benchmarked; Molmer-Sorensen two-qubit gate duration 550-883 us (median 672 us), single-qubit gate 110 us - the largest independently benchmarked all-to-all ion chain as of 2026-09-04; IonQ's Tempo (100 ions, #AQ 64) publishes no gate time [D]

ATOM-IMAGING-CYCLE-2026-09.text: Fluorescence imaging sets the neutral-atom QEC round: CZ gate 270 ns vs a 1-4.5 ms round of which imaging is 0.5-1 ms (Bluvstein et al., Nature 2025-11, 448-atom array: 0.46% bit-flip, 0.24% loss). Fast-imaging demos as of 2026-08 are not yet integrated: Kyoto/Yaqumo 17.6 us is on spinless 174Yb (occupancy discrimination, not hyperfine state readout), USTC's 15 us is an average over a 25-site subarray

MAJORANA-2018-RETRACTION.text: The founding hybrid-nanowire Majorana result, Zhang, Liu, Gazibegovic et al. (Kouwenhoven, TU Delft/Eindhoven, Microsoft-funded), "Quantized Majorana conductance", Nature 556, 74-79, published 2018-03-28, was RETRACTED on 2021-03-08 (retraction notice doi 10.1038/s41586-021-03373-x); the article page is now titled "RETRACTED ARTICLE". Any brief dating the InAs/InSb-Al hybrid-wire lineage to 2018 must carry this, since it is the reason outside groups discount later single-laboratory Majorana claims [D]

MBE-EXPORT-CONTROL-2024-09.text: Export-control position of III-V MBE growth for quantum devices as of 2026-09-04: the BIS interim final rule of 2024-09-06 created quantum-specific classifications - 3A901/3D901/3E901 (cryogenic CMOS ICs and parametric amplifiers), 3A904 (cryogenic cooling systems), 3B903 (electron microscopes for semiconductor imaging), 3B904 (cryogenic wafer probing), 4A906/4D906/4E906 (quantum computers, electronic assemblies and components), and 3C907 for EPITAXIAL MATERIALS - but no classification covering epitaxial-growth or MBE equipment itself. QUTECH-KITAEV-CITATIONS-2026.text: EXACT citations behind the QuTech independent parity-readout replication (supersedes the loose dating in QUTECH-KITAEV-READOUT-2026): (1) van Loo, Zatelli, Steffensen, Roovers et al. (QuTech/TU Delft, TU Eindhoven, CSIC Madrid), "Single-shot parity readout of a minimal Kitaev chain", Nature 650 (8101), published 2026-02-11: quantum-capacitance readout of a two-site "poor man's Majorana" Kitaev chain in InSb nanowires, random telegraph switching with lifetimes exceeding a millisecond (average ~1.85 ms), SNR ~1.93, cross-checked by rf charge sensing; (2) Zatelli, Roovers, van Loo, ... CORRDEC-ORIGIN-2024-03.text: Correlated decoding across transversal gates was introduced by Cain, Zhao, Zhou, Meister, Bonilla Ataides, Jaffe, Bluvstein, Lukin (Harvard), "Correlated decoding of logical algorithms with transversal gates", arXiv:2403.03272 (v1 2024-03-05, rev. 2025-04-07): decoding the joint syndrome history improves both Clifford and non-Clifford transversal entangling gates and reduces noisy syndrome-extraction rounds between gates from O(d) to O(1) in Clifford circuits; two decoders of differing runtime/accuracy explored; no journal reference on the arXiv record as of 2026-09-04. This is the decoding half that AFT-NATURE-2025 builds on

RL-QEC-ABSTRACT-2026-07.text: TAG CORRECTION for Sivak, Morvan, Broughton, Cortinas et al. (Google, arXiv:2511.08493 v1 2025-11-11; Nature 655, 2026-07-08). HYPERFINE-ORIGIN-1995.text: Lineage anchor for the hyperfine/clock-state qubit ("since 1995"): Monroe, Meekhof, King, Itano, Wineland (NIST Boulder), "Demonstration of a Fundamental Quantum Logic Gate", Phys. Lett. 75, 4714 (1995-12-18) - the abstract states the two qubits are stored in the internal and external degrees of freedom of a single trapped, laser-cooled atom but does NOT name the species or the hyperfine sublevels, so the hyperfine attribution rests on the wider literature, not on this abstract [D]

YB-HOUR-MEMORY-2020.text: arXiv:2008.00251 ("Single ion qubit with estimated coherence time exceeding one hour") is a SINGLE Yb ion-qubit memory: coherence beyond one hour, with non-classical information verified preserved for over 6,000 s and the decoherence process studied by quantum process tomography. The abstract does not state the isotope or name the hyperfine clock transition; ambient magnetic-field noise is identified as the challenge addressed [D]

NN-LATTICE-ORIGIN-2014.text: Barends, Kelly, Megrant, Veitia, Sank, Jeffrey, White, Mutus, Fowler, Campbell et al. (Google/UCSB, Martinis group), "Logic gates at the surface code threshold: superconducting qubits poised for fault-tolerant quantum computing", arXiv:1402.4848 (2014-02-19), Nature 508, 500 (2014): five Xmon qubits in a LINEAR ARRAY WITH NEAREST-NEIGHBOUR COUPLING, average 1Q fidelity 99.92%, 2Q up to 99.4%, five-qubit GHZ with the full gate set - the dated anchor for the static nearest-neighbour lattice (since=2014) [D]

HEAVYHEX-ORIGIN-2019.text: The heavy-hex lattice originates as a CODE construction, arXiv:1907.09528 (2019-07): "a hybrid surface/Bacon-Shor code mapped onto a (heavy) hexagonal lattice" whose lattice "includes all the ancilla qubits required for fault-tolerant error-correction", using flag qubits to correct to the full code distance under limited connectivity, and introducing both the heavy hexagon code and the heavy square code; motivation is reducing frequency collisions "by several orders of magnitude". CAUTION: the arXiv abstract page returned body text only - title, authors and journal reference remain unconfirmed [S]

GKP-QUDIT-BREAKEVEN-2025-05.text: ATTRIBUTION: the "GKP qudits beyond break-even" result is Brock, Singh, Eickbusch, Sivak, Ding, Frunzio, Girvin, Devoret at UC SANTA BARBARA and GOOGLE QUANTUM AI (not Yale), "Quantum error correction of qudits beyond break-even", Nature 641, 612-618 (2025-05-14): transmon dispersively coupled to a 3D microwave cavity; cavity T1 = 631 us, T2R = 1030 us; qutrit gain G3 = 1.82 +/- 0.03 (logical rate (886 +/- 3 us)^-1), ququart G4 = 1.87 +/- 0.03 ((620 +/- 2 us)^-1); gain = ratio of physical to logical decay rate [D]

LDPCCAT-RUIZ-2024.text: Ruiz, Guillaud, Leverrier, Mirrahimi, Vuillot, "LDPC-cat codes for low-overhead quantum computing in 2D", arXiv:2401.09541 (v1 2024-01-17, v2 2024-02-06), published Nature Communications 16, 1040 (2025): code family [165+8l, 34+2l, 22]; 758 cat qubits give 100 logical qubits at a target logical error <=10^-8 per cycle per logical qubit, ASSUMING ~0.1% phase-flip, with short-range 2D interactions and low-weight stabilizers - the source of the "100-1000x fewer qubits" claim [S]

Lett. 131, 040602 (submitted 2023-02-13, rev. 2023-08-04) - the target is the 256-bit ELLIPTIC-CURVE discrete logarithm, NOT RSA-2048; 126,133 cat qubits at an average of 19 photons, assuming a single-to-two-photon loss ratio of 1e-5 and a 500 ns cycle [S]
